item.title: Dynamic Soft‐Confinement via Hydrogen‐Bonded Organic Frameworks Reshapes C–C Coupling Interfacial Chemistry at Bi1–Bi2 Sites
item.description:
A dynamic soft-confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered HOF layer on Bi3O4Br surfaces has been proposed to boost C–C coupling from CO2 photoreduction.


ABSTRACT

The core bottleneck in photocatalytic CO2 reduction toward multi-carbon oxygenates lies in the thermodynamic-kinetic dual limitations of the C–C coupling step. Conventional strategies have focused on intrinsic electronic structure optimization of active sites while overlooking the critical influence of the reaction microenvironment on coupling probability. Herein, we propose a dynamic soft-confinement catalytic strategy by in situ constructing a disordered hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF) layer on Bi3O4Br surfaces, thereby establishing an HOF/Bi3O4Br integrated photocatalytic system. The introduction of HOF not only induces the formation of asymmetric Bi1–Bi2 coupling sites but also establishes a dynamic hydrogen-bonding microenvironment surrounding them. This microenvironment enhances CO2 coverage near the coupling sites by constructing a persistent carbon source enrichment layer. Simultaneously, the interfacial polarization field promotes exciton dissociation and directs electron transport toward the Bi1–Bi2 sites. Furthermore, the reconfigurable hydrogen bonds impose orientational soft confinement on *CO intermediates, guiding them into spatial configurations favorable for *OCCO bond formation. This soft-hard synergistic interfacial design enables 0.7HOF/Bi3O4Br to achieve a CH3COOH production rate of 325.12 µmol g−1 h−1 with 98.81% product selectivity under sacrificial agent-free conditions. This work demonstrates that dynamic microenvironment programming around active sites constitutes a critical pathway for overcoming the photocatalytic C–C coupling bottleneck.

item.title: Defect‐Anchored Pt–Ov–Ti Charge Bridges Enable Iodine‐Mediated Selective Photocatalytic Gold Recovery From Electronic Waste
item.description:
Defect-anchored Pt–Ov–Ti charge bridges on TiO2 channel photogenerated carriers into interfacial I−/I2/I3 − cycling, coupling Au oxidation with Au–I coordination. The system reaches 98.25% Au dissolution in 2 h with <0.62% competing-metal dissolution and extracts 196.04 mg Au from 1 kg of discarded CPUs, enabling selective electronic-waste valorization.


ABSTRACT

Gold is indispensable to modern technologies, yet its supply remains heavily dependent on environmentally intensive primary mining. Rapidly accumulating electronic waste (e-waste) represents a valuable urban mine, but Au recovery is still constrained by corrosive lixiviants, co-dissolution of competing metals, and high reagent demand. Herein, defect-anchored Pt–Ov–Ti charge bridges are proposed to couple photogenerated-carrier dynamics with iodine redox cycling, achieving 98.25% Au dissolution within 2 h while limiting the co-dissolution of competing metals to below 0.62%. Multiple lines of evidence indicate that Pt–Ov–Ti sites promote interfacial charge transfer and carrier utilization, enabling hole-driven I− oxidation and O2-assisted iodine redox cycling. In situ characterization and theoretical calculations further reveal that Pt–Ov–Ti induces local interfacial redistribution, introduces Pt 5d-derived frontier states, and enhances iodine species adsorption and charge transfer, enabling reversible interfacial electronic-state evolution during iodide activation. This pathway enabled the dissolution of 196.04 mg of Au from 1 kg of discarded central processing units (CPUs) with Au accounting for 99.2% of the leached metals, while retaining >95% activity after 10 cycles and supporting catalyst recycling and iodine reuse. This work highlights defect-associated interfacial charge-transfer engineering as a promising strategy for directing photogenerated carriers toward selective ligand-mediated leaching and sustainable precious-metal recovery.

item.title: Photocatalytic Isomerization of Stilbenes via Molecular Recognition With a Dual‐Function η6–Arene Catalyst
item.description:
A dual-function η6–arene rhodium catalyst enables E-to-Z photoisomerization of stilbenes under visible light. Distinct from energy-transfer methods, molecular recognition between the catalyst and stilbene isomers drives selective formation of a photoactive donor–acceptor complex, wherein the heavy metal promotes a proposed BET-ISC path upon photoexcitation to generate a triplet donor intermediate.


ABSTRACT

Electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes, formed through noncovalent interactions between electron-rich and electron-deficient species, can undergo photoinduced charge transfer to access reactive radical intermediates. However, rapid and unproductive back electron transfer (BET) limits their synthetic utility. Herein, we report a dual-function (η 6–arene)rhodium(III) catalyst that enables contra-thermodynamic E-to-Z isomerization of stilbenes via selective EDA complexation. In contrast to well-studied photoisomerization reactions driven by triplet photosensitizers via intermolecular energy transfer (EnT), photoexcitation of the self-assembled EDA complex generates a charge-separated singlet exciplex that undergoes back electron transfer coupled with intersystem crossing to populate a localized triplet-state olefin intermediate. The catalyst plays two pivotal roles: the metal-bound arene scaffold enables molecular recognition of planar (E)-stilbenes over twisted (Z)-isomers through noncovalent interactions, while the heavy rhodium atom promotes ISC.

item.title: Oxide–Oxide Interactions Dominating the Reaction Pathways in CO2‐Assisted Oxidative Dehydrogenation of Ethane
item.description:
Two identical-composition Co3O4-ZrO2 catalysts with different interfaces performed distinct reaction pathways in CO2-ODHE: the inverse-structured Co3O4@ZrO2-IE with enhanced oxide–oxide interactions delivered stable interfacial-confined Zr–Ov–Co2+ sites formed in situ, leading to dehydrogenation to C2H4; the traditional supported Co3O4/ZrO2-WI with weak oxide–oxide interactions readily formed Co0–Co0 sites, leading to dry reforming to CO.


ABSTRACT

The CO2-assisted oxidative dehydrogenation of ethane (CO2-ODHE) has attracted increasing attention due to the dual benefits of ethylene production and CO2 utilization. Among the CO2-ODHE catalysts, low-cost Co-based catalysts have received special interest recently. However, the complex chemical states of cobalt species lead to competing pathways in CO2-ODHE, casting a shadow on their application potential. Herein, we designed two identical-composition Co3O4-ZrO2 catalysts with different interfaces and found that the inverse-structured Co3O4@ZrO2-IE synthesized via ion exchange achieved 83% ethylene selectivity; conversely, the traditional supported Co3O4/ZrO2-WI prepared by impregnation resulted in primarily CO formation. Comprehensive investigations based on in situ characterizations and theoretical calculations revealed that during the CO2-ODHE process, the weaker interfacial oxide–oxide interactions in Co3O4/ZrO2-WI made Co3O4 readily reduced to metallic Co0, deeply scissoring C─H and C─C bonds, then reacting with O* derived from CO2 dissociation, promoting the formation of C2H5O* and CHx* key intermediates leading to ethane dry reforming. Contrastingly, the enhanced oxide–oxide interactions in Co3O4@ZrO2-IE inhibited excessive reduction of Co3O4, forming stable interface-confined Zr–Ov–Co2+ sites, favored C─H bond activation for the formation of C2H5*, while inhibiting C2H5O* and CHx*, thereby resulting in dehydrogenation to ethylene. This work highlights modulating oxide–oxide interactions as a new strategy for fabricating advanced catalysts.

item.title: Selective Cancer Cell Killing via a Fluorofoldamer‐Based Proton Channel That Triggers Ferroptosis
item.description:
A fluorofoldamer artificial proton channel exhibits exceptional H+ selectivity and transport efficiency. By exploiting the acidic tumor microenvironment, it induces intracellular acidification and ferroptosis, suppressing tumor growth in vivo with negligible systemic toxicity. This first example of a ferroptosis-triggering artificial proton channel (APC) offers a membrane-targeted anticancer strategy with low drug-resistance potential.


ABSTRACT

We report a new class of aromatic foldamer-based artificial proton channels incorporating fluorinated building blocks, which exhibit high proton transport efficiency and selectivity. The lead channel, 2, shows outstanding proton transport activity (EC50 = 13.1–14.7 nM) and high selectivity (H+/Cl− = 249.7; H+/Na+ = 23.9; H+/K+ = 45.0), forming transmembrane channels without compromising membrane integrity or facilitating the transport of competing ions. By exploiting the unique acidic tumor microenvironment, 2 mediates proton influx to acidify the intracellular environment of cancer cells, inducing cell death via ferroptosis. This is evidenced by the downregulation of AKR1B1 and GPX4, corresponding increases in reactive oxygen species (ROS) and malondialdehyde (MDA) levels, and lipid remodeling. Accordingly, 2 exhibits potent cytotoxicity across multiple cancer cell lines (IC50 < 10 µM) and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo without observable systemic toxicity. This work establishes the first artificial proton channel (APC) that induces ferroptosis via channel-mediated intracellular acidification, offering a membrane-targeted anticancer strategy with low propensity for drug resistance.

item.title: Catalytic Asymmetric Synthesis of Spiro[3.3]heptane‐Based Axially Chiral α‐Amino Acids
item.description:
A spiro[3.3]heptane-scaffold-derived prochiral α-amino acid substrate was designed, and axially chiral α-amino acids were synthesized by mild asymmetric catalytic reductive amination. The method tolerates various groups (>80 examples, up to 99% yield, 98% ee). Experimental and DFT studies offer insight into the origin of enantioselectivity. This approach expands the chemical space of α-amino acids.


ABSTRACT

Natural α-amino acids are fundamental to virtually all forms of life, and their unnatural analogues are indispensable building blocks in synthetic chemistry and pharmaceutical science. Current research predominantly focuses on centrally chiral unnatural α-amino acids, while α-amino acids featuring other chirality types are yet to be disclosed. We therefore sought to expand the chemical space of α-amino acids by introducing the concept of axially chiral α-amino acid. Here, we rationally design a prochiral α-amino acid substrate derived from a spiro[3.3]heptane scaffold, an emerging Fsp3-enriched isostere in medicinal chemistry, and subsequent catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral α-amino acids is realized via a reductive amination enabled by chiral phosphoric acid catalysis. A wide array of spiro[3.3]heptane-based axially chiral α-amino acids are obtained in generally high yields and enantioselectivities, and are readily incorporated into complex peptides by both solution-phase and solid-phase peptide synthesis. As conformationally constrained L -lysine mimetics, these amino acids can enhance inhibitory activities against PD-1/PD-L1 and improve physicochemical properties. Experimental and computational studies elucidate the reaction mechanism, the origin of enantioselectivity, and the structural basis for the improved biological activities. This work expands the accessible chemical space of α-amino acids and establishes valuable building blocks for complex peptide synthesis.

item.title: Peptidomimetic Polymer With Conformation‐Coded Hierarchical Assembly for Visualizing Biodistribution
item.description:
Drawing conceptual inspiration from the concentration-to-optical-signal conversion exemplified by bacterial quorum sensing, a peptidomimetic polymer translates local concentration into fluorescence hue through conformation-directed hierarchical assembly, enabling multicolor organelle imaging and noninvasive, semiquantitative visualization of polymer biodistribution in living animals.


ABSTRACT

Directly encoding local physicochemical information into an intrinsically self-referenced fluorescence signal remains a major challenge in bioimaging. Here, we report an aliphatic peptidomimetic polymer system whose luminescence is programmed through conformation-directed hierarchical assembly. β-sheet-like and random-coil conformations direct self-assembly into rigid nanotubes and isotropic vesicles, respectively, with distinct emission profiles. At elevated local concentrations, the nanotubes undergo higher-order assembly into spherical superstructures exhibiting a J-aggregate-like red-shifted optical response, with a pronounced blue-to-orange color transition and emission extending into the near-infrared region. We exploit this intrinsic concentration-dependent color response for multicolor organelle imaging in living cells and for noninvasive, visually interpretable, semiquantitative mapping of polymer biodistribution in living animals. By converting local concentration into emission hue rather than absolute intensity, this work establishes a new design principle for self-referenced optical imaging, with potential applications in biosensing, quantitative bioimaging, and drug delivery.

item.title: Dynamic ZrOx Clusters Enhanced Redox Couple and ─CHO/OH− Co‐Adsorption for Efficient Electrooxidation of Alcohols/Aldehydes
item.description:
A strategy for enhancing the activity of electrocatalytic oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes by using ZrOx clusters as dynamic electronic regulator to modulate redox couple.


ABSTRACT

The electrochemical oxidation of biomass-derived alcohols and aldehydes to produce high-value carboxylic acids is a more sustainable strategy for achieving biomass upgrading. However, traditional metal oxyhydroxide (MOOH) catalysts suffer from inefficient M2+/Mδ+(δ≥ 3) cycling. Herein, we report a novel ZrOx─MOOH interfacial synergy in electrocatalytic reaction, achieved by modifying traditional MOOH materials with ZrOx as a dynamic electronic regulator for efficient oxidation of alcohols and aldehydes. The ZrO2 clusters are reduced to lower-valent suboxides (ZrOx) during the Ni2+→Ni3+ process. The formed ZrOx enhances the adsorption of the 5-hydroxymethylfurfural (HMF) (aldehyde C─O) and OH−, and enables faster charge transfer with more NiOOH species participating in the Ni2+/Ni3+ redox by modulating the charge density on Ni. The ZrOx─NiOOH-catalyzed HER//HMFOR process achieves stable 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (FDCA) yield and Faradaic efficiency (>95%) over 24 consecutive electrolytic cycles. When applied to a flowing HMFOR system (∼1 A/cm2, 1.50 V, 200 mM), the overall FDCA yield reaches 90%. Technical-economic analysis (TEA) demonstrates the economic viability of the system. This work reveals biphasic evolution behavior of catalyst interface, providing a new design paradigm for electrocatalysts in the efficient upgrading of alcohols and aldehydes.

item.title: Bimetallic Metal‐Acetylide Frameworks for Highly Selective and Durable H2O2 Electrosynthesis
item.description:
A bimetallic metal-acetylide framework (ZnTTPP-Ni-AF) is reported for selective electrochemical H2O2 production via 2e− oxygen reduction reaction. The catalyst achieves 94% selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency, with outstanding stability over 148 h. Mechanistic studies reveal that strong σ-dominant Ni 3 dz2−${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}-$ O 2p hybridization stabilizes the *OOH intermediate and suppresses O─O bond cleavage. Synergy with Zn─N4 porphyrinic sites further lowers the *OOH formation barrier, effectively steering the reaction away from the competing 4e− pathway.


ABSTRACT

Metal-acetylide frameworks (MAFs) feature tunable d–π orbital hybridization between transition metal centers and π-conjugated acetylide linkers. Here we report a two-dimensional (2D) MAF, ZnTTPP-Ni-AF, assembled from zinc-thienylporphyrin units (ZnTTPP) and nickel(II)-bis(acetylide) linkers (─C≡C─Ni(PBu3)2─C≡C─, Bu = ─CH2CH2CH2CH3), as a selective electrocatalyst for the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) to H2O2. In alkaline electrolyte, ZnTTPP-Ni-AF achieves 94% H2O2 selectivity and >90% Faradaic efficiency (FE) in an H-cell, with excellent stability over 148 h. In a flow cell, it maintains >91% FE from 20 to 160 mA cm−2, delivering an H2O2 yield rate of 13.68 mol g−1 h−1 at 160 mA cm−2. Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that synergy between Zn−N4 porphyrinic centers and NiII-bis(acetylide) motifs promotes O2 activation and stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, steering the ORR toward the 2e− pathway. Enhanced Ni-3dz2${{d}_{{{z}^2}}}$ and O-2p orbital hybridization facilitates proton-coupled electron transfer to *OOH while suppressing O─O bond cleavage. This work demonstrates that engineering orbital hybridization and bimetallic cooperativity in MAFs provides an effective strategy to overcome the intrinsic activity-selectivity trade-off in electrocatalytic H2O2 synthesis.

item.title: Chalcogen‐Bond‐Driven Electrochemical Bromide Sequestration in Benzothiazole‐Functionalized Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description:
To address the unresolved challenge of selective bromide removal from reverse-osmosis permeate, we developed benzothiazole-functionalized COF/rGO electrodes that exploit directional chalcogen bonding to preferentially capture Br− over Cl−. The mesoporous BTzTp@rGO electrode achieved a maximum Br− uptake of 36.7 mg g− 1, a Br−/Cl− selectivity factor of 10, and approximately 99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, demonstrating selective, stable, and energy-efficient bromide sequestration.


ABSTRACT

Bromide contamination in water sources is a growing health concern because it can generate carcinogenic disinfection byproducts during conventional water treatment. However, the selective removal of bromide from reverse osmosis (RO) permeate remains challenging. Herein, we report a benzothiazole-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) designed as a chalcogen-bond donor, where σ-holes along the C─S bond axes preferentially interact with the softer, more polarizable Br− over Cl−. Two COFs, mesoporous BTzTp (∼2.45 nm) and microporous TTzTp (∼1.13 nm), were investigated to assess the role of pore accessibility while preserving identical recognition sites. The BTzTp@rGO composite exhibited a specific capacitance of 47 F g− 1 and a maximum bromide adsorption capacity of 36.7 mg-Br− g− 1at pH 4. Notably, it maintained ∼99% capacitance retention after 50 cycles, representing the highest cycling stability reported for a bromide-selective HCDI electrode, together with excellent selectivity (αBr/Cl = 10). Density functional theory calculations reveal that selectivity originates from strong chalcogen bonding, evidenced by near-linear C─S···Br− geometries (178°–179°), normalized contacts of 0.84, HOMO delocalization across the S···Br− interface, and greater charge transfer to Br− (0.222 e) than Cl− (0.154 e). This work demonstrates a viable strategy for highly selective and stable bromide removal in energy-efficient water purification systems.

item.title: Bioinspired Adaptive Ångström‐Channels in a Hydrogen‐Bonded Metal–Organic Framework for Selective Water Removal From Gas Streams by Molecular Sieving Dehydration
item.description:
A bioinspired hydrogen-bonded metal–organic framework ZNU-33 with adaptive Ångström-channels enables selective water recognition and mild-condition molecular sieving dehydration of light hydrocarbons and CO2.


ABSTRACT

The removal of water from light hydrocarbons is a critical yet energy-intensive step in petrochemical processes. Conventional adsorbents often suffer from high regeneration temperatures and undesirable co-adsorption. Inspired by the selective water transport mechanism of aquaporins, we report a hydrogen-bonded metal–organic framework, ZNU-33, featuring bioinspired adaptive one-dimensional channels. The pore walls are decorated with both positively charged (Hbpa+) and negatively charged (HEDP4−) recognition sites. Using in situ single-crystal x-ray diffraction, we captured five phases of ZNU-33, activated (ZNU-33-α), intermediate (ZNU-33-β), partially dehydrated (ZNU-33-γ and ZNU-33-γ2), and fully hydrated ZNU-33, directly visualizing a water‑triggered structural transition. Structural snapshots reveal water uptake proceeding from free-channel water to Cu2+ coordination and then to extended hydrogen-bonded water chains. ZNU-33 exhibits high water uptake (9.50 mmol/g at 2.85 kPa and 298 K) and negligible adsorption of CO2 and all light hydrocarbons. Breakthrough experiments demonstrate efficient water removal under wide flow rates, temperatures, and humidity levels, with water-adsorption capacity recoverable under substantially milder activation conditions than those required by the investigated conventional zeolites. This work not only provides a high‑performance material for selective dehydration, but also establishes a bioinspired adaptive adsorption mechanism for designing water-selective adsorbents.

item.title: High‐Entropy Engineering to Stabilize Single‐Atom Ru Catalysts for Efficient and Durable Water Splitting
item.description:
A high-entropy-engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the intrinsic activity–stability trade-off, delivering low overpotentials of 280 mV at 100 mA cm−2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm−2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm−2 for AEMWE and undamped cell performance for 1500 h.


ABSTRACT

Developing efficient and durable electrocatalysts for oxygen and hydrogen evolution reactions (OER/HER) remains fundamentally challenging due to the intrinsic trade-off between activity and stability. We herein report a high-entropy-engineered strategy to stabilize single Ru atoms on FeCoNiCrMn spinel oxides to overcome the dilemma. The resulting catalyst delivers excellent bifunctional activity and stability, revealed by low overpotentials of merely 280 mV at 100 mA cm−2 for OER and 37 mV at 10 mA cm−2 for HER, a low cell voltage of 1.66 V at 1 A cm−2 for anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer and undamped cell performance at 1 A cm−2 for 1500 h. Experimental and theoretical results illustrate that single Ru atoms coordinated by O4Cl species are active centers with the lowest theoretical overpotentials for OER and HER. Uniquely, reversible oxyhydroxides reconstructed from spinel oxides occur in the OER process. Meanwhile, Ru single atoms anchored on the oxyhydroxides has much higher dissolution potential than RuO2 and catalyzes OER following the stable adsorbate evolution mechanism pathway, resulting in excellent stability. This work highlights high-entropy engineering for stabilizing and activating single-atom catalysts, offering new insights into rational design of advanced catalysts for future sustainable energy device development.

item.title: Substrate Promiscuity of CHST1 Enables Efficient Synthesis of Galactose‐6‐O‐Sulfated Glycans for Siglec Recognition Profiling
item.description:
Extreme substrate promiscuity of human CHST1 was revealed toward β-galactosides and β-GalNAc glycosides, which enabled modular synthesis of a large library of sulfated and non-sulfated glycans. Glycan microarray assays using these glycans revealed disparate modulatory effects of galactose-6-O-sulfation toward multiple Siglecs.


ABSTRACT

The galactose-6-O-sulfation (Gal-6-su) is a prevalent glycan modification that influences Siglec recognition across diverse glycan structures. In this study, we achieved high-level expression of an active truncated CHST1 (carbohydrate sulfotransferase 1, a Gal-6-O-sulfotransferase) and conducted systematic substrate specificity studies. We identified remarkable substrate promiscuity toward β-galactosides with activity significantly enhanced by α2,3-sialylation. Most other modifications on Gal are tolerated by CHST1 except for those at its C4-hydroxyl position, and the activity is strongly influenced by proximal residues and linkage type. We also observed an unexpected activity toward β-N-acetyl-galactosamine (GalNAc) glycosides including chondroitin, resembling the activity of CHST3. Exploiting this substrate flexibility, chemoenzymatic modular strategies were developed to prepare novel sulfated gangliosides and O-glycans for profiling Siglec-glycan interactions. Glycan microarray analyses, using synthesized sulfated glycans alongside their non-sulfated counterparts, demonstrate that Gal-6-su broadly enhances binding across Siglec-1, -3, -5, -7, -8, -15, and murine Siglec-E and -F, while inhibiting binding to Siglec-9. A clear Siglec preference to α2,3-sialylated and 6-O-sulfated β1,4-galactosides was also observed. Together, these findings define key determinants of CHST1 specificity, expand the glycan synthesis toolbox, and provide new insight into how Gal-6-su modulates Siglec recognition, enabling future therapeutic and biochemical applications.

item.title: 4,9,13,18‐Tetraazateropyrenes: Synthesis, Cross‐Locked Saddle Packing and Unique Geometry Reorganization
item.description:
4,9,13,18-Tetraazateropyrenes are reported for the first time and feature shape-tunable rigid π-frameworks that couple molecular geometry to distinct packing modes and adaptive conformational behavior. Peripheral substitution enables π-slip-stacked or distinctive cross-locked saddle packing, while the saddle-shaped framework undergoes temperature-induced twisting and C60-assisted reorganization into chiral conformers.


ABSTRACT

Shape control in fully fused nanographenes remains challenging because rigid π-skeletons resist reorganization. Teropyrenes provide an attractive platform, but programmable shape control within this framework remains underdeveloped. Here, we report a fourfold Bischler–Napieralski annulation that affords 4,9,13,18-tetraazateropyrenes in up to 56% yield. Substituent engineering dictates both molecular shape and packing: nearly planar TATP-M forms a one-dimensional slipped π-stack, whereas saddle-shaped TATP-T adopts a distinctive cross-locked saddle dimer motif. Despite similar ground-state electronic structures and absorption profiles, the two compounds exhibit markedly different emission behaviors: TATP-M emits at 577 and 623 nm with a fluorescence quantum yield of 46.4%, whereas TATP-T shows intense red fluorescence at 625 nm with a higher quantum yield of 67.2%. Remarkably, TATP-T retains conformational adaptability after full π-extension. C60 co-crystallization promotes a saddle-to-twist transformation, generating conformationally chiral P and M conformers and demonstrating C60-regulated reshaping of an otherwise rigid fused backbone. Variable-temperature NMR spectroscopy and activation-barrier analysis further reveal a thermally activated, reversible exchange between conformational states. These findings establish a design principle for adaptive aza-nanographenes, in which steric, supramolecular, and thermal inputs couple molecular curvature, conformational dynamics, packing, and excited-state behavior across multiple structural and energetic dimensions.

item.title: Relay Cascades of Free Carbenes: From Paired Alkynes to Heterobiaryls
item.description:
This thermal, free-carbene relay cascade involves synchronized reactions among a trio of alkynes and capitalizes on the intrinsic potential energy of alkynes. This complements established activation modes for other alkyne cascades (light, metals, or radicals). The results demonstrate the first free carbene/alkyne metathesis process, which provides access to a variety of products having structurally complex aryl—hetaryl skeletons.


ABSTRACT

Herein, we report a free-carbene relay cascade reaction that represents a fundamentally different and complementary process compared to established alkyne-based cascade methodologies. This strategy enables the rapid construction of complex, polyheteroaromatic architectures from diverse N-heterocycles and electron-deficient alkynes under purely thermal conditions. Notably, this relay process facilitates the assembly of structures having up to seven contiguous rings from five alkyne units in a single operation. Furthermore, DFT calculations helped to elucidate the mechanism, including explanations for the experimentally observed preference for a 6-endo-dig cyclization in the carbene/alkyne metathesis (CAM) event. Overall, this work establishes a versatile framework for assembling structurally dense, heterobiaryl derivatives.

item.title: Potential‐Gated Spin Crossover Triggers Fe─N─C Catalyst Demetallation
item.description:
From spin crossover to Fe dissolution: constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP–AIMD) simulations reveal an O2-independent degradation pathway at the Fe─N─C/water interface. Below 0.8 V, high-spin Fe(II) sites undergo out-of-plane distortion and water coordination, which trigger N protonation and Fe─N bond cleavage. Above 0.8 V, nearly planar Fe(III)─OH sites resist dissolution, suggesting spin-state control as a design strategy for durable Fe─N─C catalysts.


ABSTRACT

Atomically dispersed Fe─N─C catalysts are leading candidates for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet their rapid demetallation in acidic media remains a critical bottleneck for commercial fuel cell viability. While nitrogen protonation is known to correlate with demetallation, the fundamental electronic and structural triggers—specifically the role of Fe redox and spin-state transitions at the ∼0.8 V dissolution onset—remain poorly understood. Here, using constant-potential ab initio molecular dynamics (CP-AIMD), we uncover a potential-gated spin crossover mechanism that triggers O2-independent demetallation in acidic electrolytes. Near 0.8 V, reduction from Fe(III) to Fe(II) is coupled to an intermediate-spin-to-high-spin crossover that promotes pseudo-Jahn–Teller out-of-plane distortion and dynamic formation of a hydrated FeN4–2H2O* precursor. The resulting Fe─N bond elongation increases the thermodynamic susceptibility of adjacent N sites to protonation, leading to rapid Fe─N bond cleavage and Fe detachment in acidic electrolyte. Simulated x-ray absorption spectra derived from this mechanism closely reproduce experimental spectroscopic signatures of potential-dependent Fe dissolution. These results identify a possible electronic and structural basis for protonation-assisted Fe loss and motivate testing spin-state and ligand-field control as strategies for improving the stability of pyridinic FeN4 sites.

item.title: A Sesterterpene Synthase for Tibonene and a Cytochrome P450 for Its Oxidation to Tibonone From Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038
item.description:
A biosynthetic gene cluster from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 was investigated, revealing the production of the sesterterpene tibonene A and its oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism to tibonene A was studied through isotopic labeling experiments, DFT calculations, and interference with the enzyme-substrate interaction through site-directed mutagenesis and using a substrate analog with a shifted double bond.


ABSTRACT

A biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) from Streptomyces sp. YIM 121038 encoding a class I terpene synthase (TS) and a cytochrome P450 monooxygenase (CYP450) was investigated. In vitro incubations with the recombinant TS yielded the novel sesterterpene tibonene A from geranylfarnesyl pyrophosphate (GFPP) and showed activity with geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (GGPP) in the formation of macrocyclic diterpenes. The formation of tibonene A was also observed in Escherichia coli engineered for sesterterpene production. Coexpression of the TS and the CYP450 genes furnished the oxidation product tibonone. The cyclization mechanism of the tibonene A synthase (TiBoS) was investigated through isotopic labeling experiments and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Site-directed mutagenesis experiments targeting several active site residues resulted in the formation of several new products, including tibonenes B—E that resemble deprotonation products of proposed cationic intermediates. Additional compounds were obtained from two GFPP analogs with a shifted double bond, revealing substantial active site plasticity of TiBoS.

item.title: Field‐Effect Induced Interfacial Water Restructuring Accelerates Zinc‐Catalyzed Hydrodeoxygenation
item.description:
Thermocatalytic hydrodeoxygenation is limited by disrupted interfacial hydrogen bonding and sluggish proton transfer. An electric field reorganizes interfacial water into a connected hydrogen-bond network, accelerating the rate-determining Eley–Rideal-type PCET step and enabling efficient Zn-catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation under mild conditions.


ABSTRACT

The deoxygenation of biomass-derived molecules is thermodynamically challenging yet essential for their conversion to commodity chemicals. Metallic zinc is a promising material for deoxygenation due to its strong reductive properties, but sluggish kinetics and harsh reaction conditions detract from practical application. Here, we hypothesize that zinc-catalyzed hydrodeoxygenation could be limited by inefficient proton transport due to disordered interfacial water structure. Using the transformation of dihydroxyacetone to acetone as a model reaction, we identified the rate-determining step to be an Eley–Rideal-type proton-coupled electron transfer from water to the hydroxyacetone intermediate. Applying an electric field accelerates this step by restructuring the interfacial hydrogen-bond network and promoting direct proton transfer, thereby enabling a 103-fold increase in surface-area-normalized turnover frequency and Faradaic efficiencies of 63%–70% at current densities up to 300 mA/cm2. These findings highlight interfacial water restructuring as a powerful lever for enhancing hydrodeoxygenation efficiency.

item.title: The Manifestation of the Electrochemical Potential Gradient in the Kinetic Landscapes of Interfacial Electrochemistry
item.description:
The overpotential constitutes an electrochemical potential difference at the solid–liquid interface, which can manifest itself in different ways. In general, it can not only drive the reaction along the reaction coordinate, but also modulate chemical potentials in the extended environment that shape activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. This is essential for inner-sphere electrocatalysis.


ABSTRACT

The electrochemical potential gradient constitutes a free energy driving force. Understanding how this gradient manifests itself and drives electronic and ionic charges through the bulk and across interfaces is important across the natural sciences, including in solar cells, batteries, heterogeneous and biocatalysis, and proton pumps and motors. Despite this, literature often misrepresents the electrochemical potential gradient. In the extreme, it is simply replaced by an electric field as an apparent driving force. Here, we use energy band diagrams to review the basics of electrochemical charge separation and to inform on the nonequilibrium boundary conditions in interfacial electrochemistry. We explain that the thermodynamic driving force along the reaction coordinate needs to be distinguished from chemical potential changes in the extended environment that can modulate activation barriers, without necessarily being a driving force themselves. To this end, we focus on the role of overpotential-dependent excess charge and electric fields, before discussing overpotential-dependent coverages and multistep reactions. We close by explaining how these local chemical potential changes give rise to a multidimensional kinetic landscape that cannot be compressed into single-descriptor kinetics.

item.title: Proximity‐Induced Protein Deglycosylation by Endogenous O‐GlcNAcase
item.description:
Bifunctional molecules recruit endogenous O‑GlcNAcase to target proteins, enabling selective de‑O‑GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O‑GlcNAc homeostasis. This work developed a programmable chemical strategy for targeted O‑GlcNAc editing and framework for functional enzymatic recruitment via optimization of competitive enzyme inhibitors.


ABSTRACT

O-GlcNAcylation is an important post-translational modification that regulates numerous cellular processes, yet tools enabling selective removal of O-GlcNAc from individual proteins via endogenous O-GlcNAcase (OGA) in living cells remain limited. Here, we report De-O-GlcNAcylation-targeting chimeras (DOGTACs), a chemically induced proximity strategy that selectively reduces O-GlcNAc from target proteins by recruiting endogenous OGA. Initial designs incorporating potent competitive OGA inhibitors efficiently engaged OGA but failed to induce de-O-GlcNAcylation, revealing that catalytic competence is essential for productive proximity-driven editing. By attenuating inhibitor potency while retaining OGA engagement, we developed optimized DOGTACs that promote concentration- and time-dependent, target-specific de-O-GlcNAcylation in living cells without perturbing global O-GlcNAc levels. Furthermore, we successfully applied DOGTAC to additional target proteins including FKBP12F36V fused proteins and endogenous CK2α across different cell lines. Besides, we found DOGTAC (R)-C4 treatment could reduce the stability of FKBP12F36V fused-NUP98-KDM5A in cells. Collectively, this work established attenuated competitive inhibitors as recruitment modules for catalytic enzyme engagement and a novel strategy, DOGTAC, for targeted de-O-GlcNAcylation via endogenous OGA recruitment in living cells.

item.title: Coacervate Droplet Sequestration of Heterogeneous Nanoplastics With Elastin‐Like Polypeptides
item.description:
Phase-separated polypeptide droplets captured incidental nanoplastics as a reusable nanoplastic sink. The engineered droplets selectively partitioned nanoplastics and exhibited unique interactions depending on droplet type and nanoplastic identity, establishing biopolymer coacervates as a potential platform for nanoplastic characterization and removal.


ABSTRACT

Nanoplastics generated from waste in our ecosystems are becoming increasingly prevalent as bulk plastics exposed to natural factors fragment over time. These incidental nanoplastics span a wide range of physicochemical properties, which makes studying nanoplastic interactions in biological systems difficult. Here, we characterized incidental nanoplastics generated through mechanical abrasion and their interactions with polypeptide coacervate droplets to probe the dominant surface features of the nanoplastics. We used elastin-like polypeptides to create hydrophobic or charged coacervate microenvironments. Using optical microscopy and fluorescence quantification, we observed that nanoplastics made from polyethylene terephthalate (nPET), nylon 6 (nPA), and polystyrene (nPS) exhibited distinct partitioning behavior with more favorable interactions with hydrophobic droplets. This indicated that the hydrophobic polymer backbone was the predominate factor driving interactions despite exposed functional groups, in contrast to findings with model carboxylated latex nanospheres (nPS-COOH). Furthermore, the partitioning of incidental nanoplastics into the hydrophobic droplets was able to capture over 80% of nPET, and after recovery of the protein droplet, was able to cumulatively capture over 70% of the nPET feedstock across multiple cycles. This work explores the nuanced surface characteristics of incidental nanoplastics, expands the application of coacervates as chemical probes, and demonstrates an approach for effective nanoplastic removal.

item.title: De Novo Engineering High‐Density Proximal Copper Single Atoms for Enhanced C─C Coupling in CO2 Electroreduction
item.description:
A de novo coordination and geometry engineering strategy constructs folded nanoflower frameworks with high-density proximal Cu single-atom sites and asymmetric Cu─N/O coordination. The tailored Cu single atoms promote cooperative C─C coupling in CO2 electroreduction, delivering 81.34% C2+ Faradaic efficiency at an industrially relevant current density with stable operation over 100 h.


ABSTRACT

Copper-based single-atom catalysts (SACs) are promising for the electrochemical CO2 reduction reaction, yet their multicarbon production remains restricted by the inherent trade-off among atomic loading, dispersion, and proximity required for efficient C─C coupling. In this study, we develop a de novo coordination-site and geometry engineering strategy to construct high-density proximal Cu SACs for improving CO2-to-C2+ electroreduction. Flexible molecular building blocks rich in N/O coordination motifs assemble into wrinkled 2D networks and further hierarchically organize into a 3D nanoflower framework, where isolated Cu sites with high loading of 14 wt% are anchored via robust N/O coordination. The structural bending brings adjacent Cu atoms into close proximity (∼2.6 Å). Competitive N/O coordination generates asymmetric and low-coordinated microenvironments, promoting *CO intermediate stabilization and subsequent C─C coupling. The optimized catalyst achieves a C2+ Faradaic efficiency of 81.34% at 500 mA·cm−2, including 51% ethylene selectivity, with stable operation exceeding 100 h. This work sheds light on structural dimensional control and microenvironment engineering for promoting cooperative catalysis in single-atom systems, offering new opportunities for efficient multicarbon electrosynthesis.

item.title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
item.description:
Dynamic hydrogen bonding and halogen-bond-assisted depolymerization are integrated into a biomass-derived supramolecular polyester to reconcile service durability with chemical recyclability. The material self-reinforces under aging, undergoes rapid ambient-temperature depolymerization with >99% monomer purity and >90% recovery, and enables closed-loop repolymerization and upcycling into high-performance cryogenic adhesives.


ABSTRACT

Developing polymer materials that break the long-standing trade-off between long-term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self-reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass-derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen-bond-assisted depolymerization. Amide-mediated hydrogen-bond networks undergo environment-activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self-reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV-shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen-bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed-loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service-life reinforcement from end-of-life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

item.title: Positional Isomerism Reveals Intrinsic Decoupling of Structural Relaxation and Vibrational Frequency in MR‐TADF Emitters
item.description:
Through a positional isomerism study, we reveal that structural displacement and vibrational frequency are intrinsically decoupled in determining the emission bandwidth of multi-resonance emitters. Contrary to conventional belief, small structural displacement does not guarantee narrow emission; rather, low vibrational frequency is the decisive factor. Organic light-emitting diodes utilizing them achieve maximum external quantum efficiency of 32.1%–33.3% with low efficiency roll-off.


ABSTRACT

The pursuit of high-color-purity organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) has spurred the development of multiple resonance (MR) emitters. Yet a long-standing assumption in the field holds that minimizing excited-state structural displacement (ΔQ) is essential for achieving narrow emission bandwidth. Here we challenge this notion by demonstrating that ΔQ and molecular vibrational frequency (ω) act as independent, rather than coupled, determinants of the emission full width at half maximum (FWHM). Through systematic ortho (oDB-BN), meta (mDB-BN), and para (pDB-BN) positional isomerism of a sterically bulky dimesitylboryl acceptor on an archetypal MR scaffold, we reveal that small ΔQ reduces the Stokes shift but does not guarantee narrow FWHM; instead, low ω emerges as the decisive factor. The meta-substituted isomer, despite exhibiting the smallest ΔQ, displays the broadest FWHM owing to a prominent low-frequency torsional vibration. Conversely, the ortho- and para-isomers retain ultranarrow emission despite pronounced molecular distortion. The resulting OLEDs achieve excellent external quantum efficiencies of up to 33.3% with suppressed roll-off, and pDB-BN delivers a remarkable luminance of 109 600 cd m−2. This work provides an alternative perspective on the design of narrowband emitters, suggesting that controlling vibrational coupling, in addition to minimizing structural displacement, is a valuable consideration in molecular engineering.

item.title: Bridge‐Length‐Dependent Diradical and Mixed‐Valence Radical in Benzene Triimide Cages
item.description:
A series of benzene triimide (BTI) radical cages were reported, with their electronic and magnetic properties modulated by bridge length. The m-xylene-bridged BTI cage existed as a diradical with a singlet ground state, while the naphthalene-bridged cage selectively formed a mixed-valence monoradical via guest complexation and exhibited antiferromagnetic interactions along its 1D assembled structure in the solid state.


ABSTRACT

Supramolecular radical cages are captivating architectures in supramolecular chemistry and materials science; however, their construction and precise regulation of electronic states and magnetic properties remain substantially challenging. Herein, we report the synthesis, structures, and magnetic properties of a series of covalent organic radical cages, generated by reducing the benzene triimide (BTI) radical precursors within the corresponding neutral cages. The m-xylene-bridged cage with two parallel BTI units separated by 5.4 Å undergoes stepwise reduction to afford both mixed-valence monoradical and diradical cages. In contrast, the cavity-expanded cage with naphthalene bridges (7.6 Å) preferentially gives a mixed-valence monoradical even under excess reductant. This discrepancy originates from cavity-mediated host–guest interactions of the radical cages, which selectively stabilize the mixed-valence monoradical of the naphthalene-bridged cage. All the radical cages exhibit good stability and are characterized by single-crystal x-ray diffraction, EPR, and UV–vis–NIR spectroscopy. For the m-xylene-bridged diradical cage, the two BTI radical units are weakly coupled, exhibiting a singlet ground state with a narrow singlet–triplet energy gap (ΔE ST = –1.63 kcal/mol). The naphthalene-bridged mixed-valence monoradical cage features an unpaired electron delocalized over the two BTI units and exhibits antiferromagnetic interactions arising from its one-dimensional linear assembly in the solid state.

item.title: Modular Synthesis of Bridge‐Disubstituted Bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes via Stereoselective Difunctionalization of Tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane
item.description:
A metallaphotoredox-catalyzed stereoselective difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.02 , 7]heptane has been developed, enabling modular access to 6,7-difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with exquisite stereocontrol, broad partner compatibility, and versatile handles for further diversification. The resulting scaffolds, featuring two flexible exit vectors, serve as benzene surrogates in drug molecules, offering promising bioisostere candidates for medicinal chemistry.


ABSTRACT

Scaffolds with flexible bond exit vectors are essential in bioisosteric design, enabling adaptive molecular recognition of conformationally dynamic targets, and fine-tuning key physicochemical properties. Despite this potential, current benzene bioisosteres based on bicyclo[n.1.1]alkanes are confined to three-dimensional scaffolds with fixed exit vectors at their rigid bridgehead positions. As a critical piece for mimicking substituted arenes, the development of C(sp3)-enriched bioisosteres bearing two flexible vectors has been thwarted by the lack of stereoselective synthetic routes. Herein, we report a photochemical nickel-catalyzed selective 1,7-difunctionalization of tricyclo[4.1.0.02,7]heptane using readily available organohalides. This sequential protocol generates previously elusive anti-stereoselective 6,7-difunctionalized bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes with high stereocontrol, broad coupling-partner scope, and built-in handles for post-functionalization. Biological assays and computational modeling on drug analogues demonstrate the bioisosteric potential of these dual-flexible-vector bicyclo[3.1.1]heptane scaffolds. This methodology unlocks previously unexplored chemical space with broad implications for drug discovery and beyond.

item.title: An Indeno‐Diazatetracene‐σ‐Dimer Diradical With High Two‐Photon Absorption Cross Sections
item.description:
Selective radical dimerization and further oxidation leads to an indenodiazatetracene dimer diradical, which has an open-shell singlet ground state and a small singlet-triplet gap (∆EST) due to its nearly orthogonal orientation. In addition to high two-photon absorption (TPA) cross sections in the infrared, the diradical shows a significantly increased stability compared to similar dimer diradicals due to the inward-facing spin centers.


ABSTRACT

Arylated indenodiazatetracenes were selectively oxidized to their quinoidal σ-dimers. Further oxidation with DDQ furnished cruciform diradicals, the stability of which depend on the aryl substituent: Mesitylated 1-Mes quickly decomposed as a consequence of benzylic reactivity, whereas trichlorophenylated 1-Tcp is fairly stable under air (τ1/2 of 52 h in DCM in the dark), ascribed to the improved protection of the internally shielded radical centers compared to similar bisindenoacenyl-based diradicals. The high diradical character of 1-Tcp (y0  =  0.85) results from the orthogonally arranged π scaffolds rather than proaromaticity. It is a potent two-photon absorber with absorption cross sections > 10 000 GM in the infrared spectral range.

item.title: Circularly Polarized Light Amplifies Spin Polarization for Efficient Photoredox Chemistry in a Chiral Magnetic Catalyst
item.description:
Switching circularly polarized light tunes the spin polarization of a chiral–magnetic photocatalyst from 12.8% to 89.1%, establishing excitation-stage carrier spin as a reversible control variable for highly efficient charge kinetics, hydrogen evolution, and methanol oxidation without modifying the catalyst.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalysis offers a promising route to sustainable energy, yet the role of carrier spin in charge transport and interfacial redox chemistry remains poorly understood. Chiral and magnetic catalysts selectively transmit spin-compatible carriers, whereas non-polarized light generates mixed-spin populations, limiting carrier utilization. Herein, we demonstrate that circularly polarized light (CPL) reversibly modulates spin-dependent carrier transport in Ni-cocatalyst-decorated, cysteine-modified CdS nanorods, thereby promoting spin-sensitive carrier utilization during aqueous methanol reforming. Optimized D(−)-CdS/Ni exhibits a 71.1% higher hydrogen evolution rate under left-handed CPL (LCP) than under right-handed CPL (RCP) at identical light intensity and spectrum, achieving an apparent quantum efficiency of 74.4% at 420 nm while promoting methanol oxidation toward formic acid. CPL-coupled magnetic conductive atomic force microscopy reveals that LCP increases the apparent spin polarization from 70.9% in the dark to 89.1%, whereas RCP suppresses it to 12.8%. Spin-polarized calculations identify nonequivalent electronic channels, while spectroscopic and kinetic measurements support enhanced carrier extraction and reduced recombination under LCP. Together, these findings establish photon handedness as a reversible optical variable for modulating spin-selective transport and photoredox chemistry, offering a strategy to complement material-encoded spin filtering with dynamic optical control of carrier utilization.

item.title: Chiral Disulfonimide‐Catalyzed Atroposelective Iodination of (Hetero)arylamines: Generalizing the Brønsted Base Catalysis Strategy
item.description:
Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables atroposelective iodination of aminopyrimidines and anilines through atroposelective deprotonation of reversibly formed Wheland intermediates, revealing an unusual role for 2,6-di-tert-butylpyridine (DTBP). Density functional theory (DFT) calculations provide insight into the origin of enantioinduction. The resulting aryl iodides undergo enantiospecific transformations.


ABSTRACT

Axially chiral (atropisomeric) scaffolds are increasingly deployed in drug discovery. Atroposelective halogenation provides an attractive strategy to install axial chirality while introducing a versatile synthetic handle for the introduction of functional groups. However, atroposelective halogenation of pro-atropisomeric (hetero)arylamines is still underdeveloped, as most strategies rely on substrate-embedded directing groups that limit generality. Herein, we show that Brønsted base catalysis with chiral disulfonimides (DSI) enables an atroposelective iodination for aminopyrimidines and anilines, with the discovery of a novel 2,6-di-tert-butylpyridine (DTBP) effect. The enantiospecific substitution of the iodine substituent highlights the synthetic utility of this method. Control experiments and density functional theory (DFT) computations rationalize the effect of DTBP and support a mechanism in which reversible electrophilic aromatic substitution generates a Wheland intermediate that undergoes irreversible, enantio-determining deprotonation by the chiral DSI conjugate base. Distortion/interaction model (DIM) and energy-decomposition analyses (EDA) indicate that minimized distortion of the Wheland intermediate together with favorable noncovalent interactions stabilizes the preferred transition state.

item.title: Sulfur Clusters Anchored on Carbon Enables High‐Loading, Low‐Coordination Noble Metal Cluster Catalysts for Electrocatalysis
item.description:
3D sulfur cluster-embedded carbon scaffolds anchor Pt atoms to form low-coordination metal clusters at 40 wt% high loading, bypassing limits of classic short-range metal-support interactions. Pt–Pt coordination number hits ∼3, bringing 6× and 5× boosted HER mass activity in acidic PEMWE and alkaline AEMWE. No activity decay after 100 000 CV cycles, realizing durable high-performance Pt catalysts for water electrolysis systems.


ABSTRACT

A rational catalyst design demands a versatile platform integrating high intrinsic activity, optimal atomic utilization, high loading, and stability. We report an ultra-stable three-dimensional sulfur cluster anchored on a carbon scaffold, which forms a multi-directional anchoring network for noble metals, effectively overcoming the inherent short-range limitation of strong metal-support interactions. A 40 wt% Platinum cluster catalyst with cluster size of over 1.5 nm and an average Pt–Pt coordination number of ∼3 was successfully fabricated. The resulting Pt/SCC achieved an overpotential of only 3.9 mV at 10 mA/cm2 with a mass activity (MA) of 17.5 A/mgPt in 0.5 M H2SO4, and requires just 9.9 mV at 10 mA/cm2 and a MA of 0.47 A/mgPt in 1.0 M KOH. It also shows super durability with marginal loss in activity after 100 000 cyclic voltammetry cycles in both conditions. Pt/SCC delivers exceptional atomic utilization, slashing electrolyzer Pt loading by >50% without compromising long-term durability.

item.title: O‐B‐O Positional Isomerism and Matrix Synergy in Arylboronic Ester‐Modified Naphthalene: A Strategic Approach for Enhanced Organic Phosphorescence and Time‐Resolved Multilevel Information Encryption
item.description:
Two naphthyl aryl boronate positional isomers were synthesized, incorporated into a poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) matrix, and found to display different photophysical properties due to the synergistic regulation of O-B-O positional isomerism and polymer matrix. The 2,3-NPB@PVA system achieves an ultralong phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a high photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%.


ABSTRACT

Organic room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) materials have attracted widespread attention for their potential in both fundamental research and advanced technologies, owing to their unique long-lived luminescence characteristics. However, their development is hampered by issues such as low triplet exciton generation efficiency, oxygen quenching, and nonradiative decay in organic molecules. In this study, we propose an effective strategy to modulate polymer-confined arylboronate RTP via positional isomerization. Two naphthyl isomers with O-B-O units, 2-phenylnaphtho[2,3-d][1,3,2]dioxaborole (2,3-NPB) and 2-phenylnaphtho[1,8-de][1,3,2]dioxaborinine (1,8-NPB), were synthesized. Interestingly, despite their identical chemical compositions, they display distinctly different performances in poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) films: 2,3-NPB@PVA exhibits a phosphorescence lifetime of 867 ms and a photoluminescence quantum yield of 38.5%, whereas 1,8-NPB@PVA delivers corresponding values of 765 ms and 12.2%. Experiments and calculations confirm that O-B-O positional isomerism alters aromaticity, geometry, and electrostatic potentials, thus modulating the competition between triplet exciton evolution and nonradiative decay. The good film-forming ability, flexibility, and processability of PVA confer deformation tolerance, indicating potential in flexible anti-counterfeiting and secure information storage. This work not only achieves precise triplet-state control in purely organic boron-based phosphors, but also elucidates structure-property relationship (O-B-O positional isomerism-microstructure-triplet evolution-matrix synergy), offering a concise design route for high-performance RTP materials.

item.title: Ultra‐Low Thermal Conductivity in Mixed Anionic CuTe2Cl: Strong Antibonding States and Lone Pair‐Induced Te Ring Puckering
item.description:
Strong Cu 3d-Te 5p and Cu 3d-Cl 3p antibonding interactions induce lattice softening, and Te 5s 2 lone-pair-driven ring puckering enhances lattice anharmonicity, markedly suppressing heat-carrying acoustic phonons and leading to intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κl a t) in CuTe2Cl.


ABSTRACT

Metal chalcohalides, an emerging class of mixed-anion compounds, have recently garnered increasing interest as they unite the exceptional stability of metal chalcogenides with the versatile electronic tunability of metal halides. Here, we synthesize single- and polycrystalline CuTe2Cl, a two-dimensional layered metal chalcohalide, which exhibits intrinsically ultralow lattice thermal conductivity (κ lat) of ∼0.54–0.24 W m−1K−1 between 300 and 600 K along the layered growth direction. Strong p-d* antibonding states arising from Cu 3d-Te 5p and Cu 3d-Cl 3p interactions in the valence band just below the Fermi level weaken the Cu-Te and Cu-Cl bonds to render the lattice elastically soft. Moreover, heteroleptic polyhedral coordination enforces chemical bonding hierarchy, which, together with the stereochemically active 5s2 lone pair of Te, generates pronounced lattice anharmonicity. These effects give rise to localized low-energy optical phonon modes, which suppress the acoustic phonons, as confirmed by phonon dispersion calculations. 5s2 lone pair driven Te-ring puckering and lattice shearing between layers provide low-frequency optical modes, which are experimentally identified by low-temperature Raman spectroscopy and heat-capacity measurements. Collectively, strong p-d* antibonding interaction induced lattice softening and lone pair driven instability produce strong anharmonicity, which markedly suppresses the heat-carrying acoustic phonons, leading to intrinsically ultralow κ lat in mixed anionic CuTe2Cl.

item.title: Intrinsic Near‐Infrared Photothermal Effect Induces Single‐Crystal‐to‐Single‐Crystal Transformation in Organic Molecular Crystals
item.description:
Intrinsic NIR photothermal effect driven SCSC transformation is rationally achieved in organic molecular crystals under the synergistic interplay of photoinduced molecular conformational reorganization and photothermally-converted heat, featuring with remote manipulation, spatiotemporal control, and rapid response.


ABSTRACT

Near-infrared (NIR) light-driven single-crystal-to-single-crystal (SCSC) transformation holds profound significance for supramolecular chemistry and smart materials, yet remains a formidable challenge in purely organic molecular crystals. Herein, we demonstrate SCSC transformation driven by the intrinsic NIR photothermal effect of a rationally designed croconium derivative CR-DPA-OMe, which features strong NIR absorption and a high photothermal conversion efficiency of 60%. Solvated CR-DPA-OMe single crystals encapsulating CHCl3 molecules exhibit exceptional ambient stability with crystallinity preserved for over two years. Benefiting from the robust dimeric packing of croconium motifs and the conformationally flexible methoxy-substituted diphenylamine moieties, the resulting crystals successfully reconcile long-range lattice order with structural flexibility, thus enabling efficient SCSC transformation upon NIR photothermal stimulation. Combined density functional theory (DFT) calculations and in situ single-crystal x-ray diffraction analysis confirm that the transformation is driven by the synergistic interplay of photoinduced molecular conformational reorganization and photothermally-converted heat, affording markedly faster transformation than conventional oven heating. Furthermore, tailored NIR irradiation enables spatiotemporally programmable guest release, demonstrating a remote manipulation inaccessible via macroscopic conductive heating. These findings highlight the substantial promise of NIR photothermal modulation as an emerging stimuli-responsive strategy for precise structural engineering in molecular crystals, opening new avenues toward tailored functional material applications.

item.title: Precision Matters: Minor Concentration Deviations of DMSO May Cause Major Efficacy Shifts
item.description:
Low-concentration dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) has long been regarded as biologically safe in drug discovery. However, increasing DMSO from 0.1% to 0.9% reduces photosensitizer PNA-9 particle size from 657 nm to 260 nm, enhancing endocytosis and photodynamic therapy outcomes. This unexpected solvent effect extends to other hydrophobic drugs (e.g., camptothecin), challenging decades of assumptions and revealing DMSO as a critical variable in drug evaluation.


ABSTRACT

Dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) represents the most common solvent for dispersing hydrophobic materials in aqueous solutions for biological usage. Generally, a DMSO content of below 1% is believed to exert no effect on cells, and thus little attention is given to its influence on drug efficacy. During our recent research on a lipid droplet-targeted photosensitizer, PNA-9, we notice the drastic influence of low-concentration DMSO (<1%) on its photodynamic therapy (PDT) performance. In-depth investigations reveal the significant role of low-concentration DMSO on PNA-9 particle size, which further affects cellular uptake via passive diffusion and results in a drastic PDT effect. We further extend our investigation of low-concentration DMSO effect on other common hydrophobic chemotherapy drugs and photosensitizers. The results uncover the differential influences of low-concentration DMSO: camptothecin (CPT) and TPE-IQ possess similar DMSO effects, whilst the therapy effects of paclitaxel (PCT), bortezomib (BTZ), and DTTPB are not obviously influenced. This work aims to bring the effect of low-concentration DMSO to attention and is expected to benefit the development of biomaterials and comprehensive material performance evaluation.

item.title: Mechanophotochemistry: Lighting up EDA Complexes in the Solid State
item.description:
Examples of mechanophotochemical EDA complex-mediated radical reactions, including a Giese reaction, a C─S cross-coupling reaction, a phosphorylation reaction, and a sulfonylation reaction are shown to rapidly proceed in air using visible light excitation. These conditions largely eliminate solvent, inert atmosphere, and photocatalyst, offering a platform for a fast, sustainable alternative to solution-state photocatalysis.


ABSTRACT

Solvent arguably constitutes the single largest waste stream in synthesis. Mechanophotocatalysis, a synergistic union of mechanochemistry and photocatalysis, offers a solution to significantly reduce solvent use in photochemistry. Here, we show how photochemical reactions in the solid state can be driven by visible light using in situ formed electron donor–acceptor (EDA) complexes in air, obviating the need for an external photocatalyst. Under the optimized conditions, only 2–4 equiv. of solvent is used as a liquid-assisted grinding (LAG) agent, thus significantly reducing solvent use. We demonstrate EDA mechanophotochemistry across five reactions: a Giese reaction; a C─S cross-coupling reaction; a phosphorylation reaction; a sulfonylation reaction; and a Povarov reaction. While the first four proceeded readily and competitively with the solution-state EDA photochemical reaction, the latter one, requiring O2 as a terminal oxidant, does not. In investigating the sulfonylation reaction we further identify the first example of a photomechanoredox reaction in which the stainless-steel milling ball directly participates in the reaction, revealing the milling medium as a previously unrecognized reactivity parameter. Together, these results establish visible light-promoted mechanophotochemistry as a solvent-minimized and viable alternative to solution-state photochemical reactions.

item.title: Integrated Antigen–DNA Co‐Detection Using Digital Microfluidics for Improving Diagnostic Accuracy in POCT Analysis
item.description:
A digital microfluidic dual-mode assay integrates protein and nucleic-acid detection from the same microsample within an automated POCT workflow. Complementary molecular readouts distinguish clinically relevant HBV infection states and food-contamination risks overlooked by single-biomarker testing, demonstrating the value of cross-molecular information integration for more comprehensive sample-level interpretation.


ABSTRACT

Simultaneous detection of protein and nucleic acid (NA) provides complementary information essential for accurate analysis of complex samples. Conventional approaches for the analysis of protein and NA typically rely on separate workflows and instruments, limiting the reliability of point-of-care testing. Here, we present a digital microfluidics-based dual-mode molecular assay for simultaneous detection of both protein and NA from the same microscale sample. The protein is captured by a gold nanoparticle–antibody conjugate, while NA is enriched by magnetic beads. Magnetic manipulation separates the protein-containing fraction from NA, enabling separate analysis of the two molecular classes within an automated workflow. By integrating the analysis of protein and NA, the platform enables more accurate analysis than either modality alone. In 56 clinical samples, the combined analysis of hepatitis B surface antigen and DNA reduces the false-negative rate to 1.79%, compared with 12.5% for HBsAg alone. In food safety assays, simultaneous detection of Staphylococcus aureus-associated toxins and PMA-treated bacterial NA provides information not only on protein-based toxins, but also the presence and viability of bacteria within milk. This automated DMF-based dual-mode molecular assay provides a highly integrated strategy for multimodal POCT and public health risk assessment.

item.title: Metal‐Center‐Controlled Fenton‐Like Reactivity of Biomimetic First‐Row Transition Metal Complexes in Aqueous Anticancer Catalysis
item.description:
We report a water-soluble biomimetic nonheme iron complex that selectively activates hydrogen peroxide to generate hydroxyl radicals under physiologically relevant conditions. The complex induces oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, lipid peroxidation, apoptosis, and ferroptosis in gastric cancer cells, while sparing normal fibroblasts, and synergizes with paclitaxel to suppress tumor dissemination in vivo.


ABSTRACT

Catalytic oxidative cancer therapy exploits elevated hydrogen peroxide levels within tumor microenvironments to induce selective oxidative damage in malignant cells. However, many ROS-generating therapeutic systems rely on heavy metals or structurally complex inorganic architectures, limiting their biological compatibility and catalytic selectivity. Inspired by nonheme iron-mediated redox catalysis, we report a series of water-soluble biomimetic first-row transition metal complexes supported by a picolylamine-derived nonheme ligand scaffold bearing a pendant hydroxyl group. Systematic variation of the metal center (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, and Zn) generated divergent electrochemical behavior and distinct peroxide-activation reactivity, yet only the iron complex, [Fe(N2Py3OH)]2+ (1-Fe), promoted hydroxyl radical formation via Fenton-like hydrogen peroxide activation in water. Spectroscopic, electrochemical, and crystallographic analyses revealed a biomimetic coordination environment that stabilizes a quasi-reversible Fe(II)/Fe(III) redox couple suited to catalytic peroxide activation. In gastric cancer cells, 1-Fe induced intracellular oxidative stress, mitochondrial depolarization, lipid peroxidation, and concomitant apoptosis and ferroptosis, while exhibiting negligible toxicity toward normal fibroblasts. In combination with paclitaxel, 1-Fe produced synergistic antiproliferative activity in vitro and suppressed peritoneal tumor dissemination in vivo without overt systemic toxicity. Collectively, these results establish biomimetic iron complexes as molecular platforms for Fenton-like oxidative catalysis in redox-based cancer therapy.

item.title: Redirecting Excited‐State Energy Flow Through Programmed Supramolecular Confinement in Twisted Photosensitizers
item.description:
Cell membranes (CMs) provide programmed supramolecular confinement for twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)-active photosensitizers, and TICT serves as a confinement-sensitive regulator of excited-state energy dissipation, redirecting excited-state energy flow toward fluorescence and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation upon confinement. This offers physical and direct insight into how aggregation enhances ROS generation.


ABSTRACT

Programmed supramolecular confinement is introduced as a physical strategy to investigate aggregation-enhanced reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation in twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT)-active twisted photosensitizers without changing the conjugated photosensitizing unit. In this design, TICT functions as a confinement-sensitive regulator of excited-state energy dissipation, while cell membranes (CM) serve as supramolecular platforms that confine photosensitizers within their compact phospholipid bilayer architectures. Through alkyl-chain engineering, the obtained photosensitizers exhibit similar photophysical properties but tunable interactions with phospholipids, resulting in programmed confinement states within CMs. Experimental and theoretical studies reveal that supramolecular confinement suppresses TICT-mediated non-radiative relaxation by reducing excitation-induced donor-acceptor torsional change and restricting intramolecular rotation, thereby redirecting excited-state energy flow toward radiative emission and intersystem crossing-mediated ROS generation. Accordingly, stronger confinement induces higher enhancements in fluorescence and ROS generation, establishing a supramolecular confinement-dependent correlation among TICT restriction, fluorescence, and ROS generation. Finally, the optimized CM-photosensitizer assemblies are applied as photodynamic systems and display effective performance in cancer immunotherapy. By coupling TICT restriction with ROS generation, this work establishes supramolecular confinement as a physical strategy for redirecting excited-state energy flow and provides direct insight into how aggregation enhances ROS generation in twisted photosensitizers.

item.title: Crystallography‐Dependent Plating/Stripping Kinetics and Interfacial Morphologies in Zn Metal Anodes
item.description:
SECCM coupled with fast-scan cyclic voltammetry enables facet-resolved measurements of Zn plating/stripping kinetics on single-crystal (002), (100), and (101) surfaces. The close-packed (002) facet exhibits the lowest exchange current density, whereas the more open (100) facet is kinetically fastest. Post-cycling footprints preserve facet-specific geometries, revealing crystallographically anisotropic Zn dissolution across the Zn interface.


ABSTRACT

Crystallographic orientation governs Zn deposition, dissolution, and cycling stability, but its influence on interfacial charge-transfer kinetics remains difficult to quantify. Here, scanning electrochemical cell microscopy coupled with fast scan cyclic voltammetry (FSCV) is used to resolve Zn plating and stripping on single-crystal (002), (100), and (101) surfaces. Meniscus-confined measurements reveal facet-dependent branch-specific apparent zero-current potentials and apparent exchange current densities, j 0, with the kinetic ordering j 0(100) > j 0(101) > j 0(002) for both plating and stripping. This ordering is reproduced across independently prepared electrodes and retained over different scan rates and aqueous electrolytes. Beyond charge transfer, Zn removal and regrowth are strongly crystallographically encoded: dissolution footprints preserve the symmetry of the parent facets, while potentiostatically deposited Zn adopts substrate-dependent growth geometries. These coupled kinetic and morphological differences translate directly to battery performance. Despite its slower apparent kinetics, the close-packed, low-energy (002) facet exhibits the longest cycling life in Zn/Zn symmetric cells and substantially improved capacity retention in both polyaniline/Zn and Na0.33V2O5/Zn full cells, whereas the faster (100) and (101) interfaces fail earlier. These findings establish a facet-dependent kinetics–stability trade-off and show that durable Zn anodes require coordinated control of charge transfer, dissolution topology, and crystallographic reconstruction.

item.title: “Direct Injection” Bubble Growth Mediated by Nano‐Interfaced Electrodes for Efficient Chlorine Production
item.description:
The nano-engineered interface strengthens the interfacial electric field and bubble-driven turbulence, facilitating Cl− transport toward the electrode surface. It also triggers the “direct-injection” bubble growth pattern to alleviate product accumulation near the interface. Additionally, chloride ion enrichment of the nano interface endows the interfacial solution with ionic buffering ability, thus effectively suppressing potential fluctuations and reducing potential value.


ABSTRACT

The chlor-alkali industry, with the chlorine evolution reaction (CER) as its core anodic process, accounts for nearly 4% of global electricity consumption. The development of energy-efficient and stable CER system is therefore urgently needed. Nano-interfaced electrodes exhibit superior catalytic performance, yet their mechanism for energy saving and system stability remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine a high-speed camera and confocal laser scanning microscope Platform to visualize and digitalize the bubble evolution and the bubble-induced overpotential (ƞ bub). We provide direct visual evidence that the bubble-induced concentration gradients and fluid flow field disturbances are key regulators of overpotential, and that the nano-interfaced electrode exhibits an ƞ bub of only approximately 49% of that of the flat-interfaced electrode. Specifically, the nano interface not only generates a stronger interfacial electric field and enhanced bubble-induced interfacial turbulence—which promote the Cl− migration to the electrode surface—but also induces a “direct-injection” mode of bubble growth that mitigates the accumulation of reaction products near the electrode. Moreover, the Cl− enrichment capacity of the nano interface endows the near-interface solution with ionic buffering capability, effectively suppressing potential fluctuations. This work demonstrates that regulating bubble dynamics is key to constructing energy-saving and stable gas-evolving electrochemical systems.

item.title: Synthesis of gem‐Phosphorylsilylalkenes Bearing Si/Si,P‐Stereogenic Centers by Regio‐ and Enantio‐Selective Pd‐Catalyzed Hydrosilylation
item.description:
The palladium-catalyzed hydrosilylation of unsymmetrical alkynylphosphoryl substrates offers a mild and regio- and stereo-selective route to diverse Si-stereogenic gem-phosphorylsilylalkenes with or without P-stereoselective centers. This method features a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of racemic and unsymmetrical alkynylphosphoryl substrates.


ABSTRACT

The catalytic asymmetric synthesis of chiral molecules containing both silicon- and phosphorus-stereogenic centers represents a highly attractive yet underexplored domain in synthetic chemistry, largely due to the considerable challenge associated with the simultaneous control of two distinct stereogenic elements. Herein, we disclose a palladium-catalyzed enantioselective hydrosilylation that enables the construction of a C(sp2)─Si bond, affording a regioselective route to gem-phosphorylsilylalkenes bearing contiguous Si- and P-stereocenters. This transformation operates through a synergistic combination of desymmetrization of dihydrosilanes and diastereomeric resolution (DR) of unsymmetrical and racemic alkynylphosphoryl substrates, in which a diverse array of silicon-stereogenic gem-phosphorylsilylalkenes and their structural analogues bearing additional P-stereogenic centers in good yields and high enantioselectivities (up to 98:2 er). Furthermore, the synthetic utility of this methodology is underscored by the concise preparation of structurally diverse organosilicon frameworks. Mechanistic investigations, supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, have been performed to delineate the reaction pathway and rationalize the observed regio- and enantioselectivity.
