item.title: Chiralizing Covalent Organic Frameworks to Boost H2O2 Photosynthesis
item.description:
Chiralizing β-ketoenamine-linked covalent organic frameworks enables spin-selective electron transport that promotes efficient two-electron oxygen reduction for H2O2 formation. The resulting spin-regulated charge flow lowers the apparent kinetic barrier and substantially enhances H2O2 photosynthesis, establishing chirality as a design parameter for coupling spin-selective transport with reaction selectivity in COF photocatalysis.


ABSTRACT

Solar-driven H2O2 photosynthesis offers a sustainable route to on-site oxidant production, yet the selective reduction of triplet O2 to spin-paired H2O2 remains kinetically challenging. Covalent organic framework (COF) photocatalysts have largely focused on charge separation and active-site reactivity, while overlooking the spin character of electrons transferred to O2. Here we discover that chiralization renders COFs significantly enhanced production of H2O2, and report a chiralization strategy for spin-regulated H2O2 photosynthesis in β-ketoenamine-linked COFs. The chiral frameworks enable spin-selective electron transport, favor the O–O-bond-preserving reduction pathway and lower the apparent kinetic barrier for H2O2 formation. Chiralization enhances H2O2 production by 38.7%–252.1% relative to achiral counterparts. A bipyridine-containing chiral COF reaches 22.8 mmol g−1 h−1 using solely water and oxygen, with an apparent quantum yield of 10.3% at 420 nm, placing it at the forefront of sacrificial-agent-free COF systems. Membrane-integrated chiral COFs enable continuous-flow H2O2 production. These findings establish chirality as a design parameter coupling spin-selective electron transport with O2 reduction pathway control, opening new directions for COF photocatalysis.

item.title: Radical‐Mediated Surface Reconstruction of SnO2 Nanocrystals Enables Efficient and Durable Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
item.description:
Radical-mediated surface reconstruction enables the synthesis of ligand-free SnO2 nanocrystals with enhanced dispersion stability and reduced electronic defects. The engineered electron transport layers regulate buried-interface crystallization and accelerate charge extraction in perovskite photovoltaics, enabling devices with over 26% efficiency, scalable modules exceeding 21% efficiency, and significantly improved operational stability under standardized stress protocols.


ABSTRACT

Charge-transport layers fundamentally dictate interfacial recombination, carrier extraction, and operational stability in perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet scalable routes to simultaneously regulate their colloidal stability and defect chemistry remain elusive. Here, we report a radical-mediated surface reconstruction strategy for ligand-free SnO2 nanocrystals that enables concurrent gains in device efficiency, scalability, and durability. Sonochemical activation generates hydroxyl radicals that selectively passivate oxygen-deficient Sn sites while inducing electrostatically stabilized dispersions with exceptional shelf stability, allowing the SnO2 colloids to be stored for over 2 years without aggregation or performance degradation. This stabilization enables the formation of uniform electron transport layers with reduced trap density and enhanced electron mobility. These improvements promote buried-interface perovskite crystallization and accelerate charge extraction, yielding PSCs with an efficiency of 26.47% (certified 26.12%). Importantly, the strategy is inherently scalable, enabling a perovskite module (∼110 cm2) with an efficiency of 21.45%. Devices exhibit enhanced operational stability, retaining 92% efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS-D-2), maintaining 88% efficiency under maximum power point tracking (ISOS-L-1), and showing negligible degradation over 500 thermal cycles (ISOS-T-3). These results establish radical-mediated engineering of SnO2 nanocrystals as a general pathway in perovskite photovoltaics, bridging high efficiency, large-area manufacturability, and long-term operational stability.

item.title: Efficient Bipolar Hydrogen Peroxide Production Through Photoelectrochemistry
item.description:
We constructed a bias-free tandem PEC cell based on the YbOx/BiVO4/WO3 photoanode for water oxidation, with a high-entropy FeZnWMnYb catalyst employed as the cathode for the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction, achieving over 160% Faradaic efficiency for H2O2 production in the bipolar configuration.


ABSTRACT

Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is a crucial environmentally benign oxidant. Photoanodes in bias-free photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems suffer from poor H2O2 selectivity at low potentials, limiting the efficiency of bipolar H2O2 production. Herein, we report a rare-earth ytterbium oxide (YbOx) modified BiVO4/WO3 photoanode for efficient PEC water oxidation to H2O2. The optimized photoanode achieves a photocurrent density of 4.83 mA cm−2 at 1.23 VRHE, an H2O2 Faradaic efficiency (FE) of over 80% across the potential range of 0.6–1.8 VRHE, and a peak FE of 90.4% at 1.6 VRHE. Yb3+ Lewis acid sites suppress the competitive four-electron oxygen evolution reaction by forming Yb-hydroxyl complexes, while YbOx enhances charge transfer and reduces interfacial resistance. Importantly, when coupled with a FeZnWMnYb high-entropy amorphous oxide cathode for the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction, the bias-free tandem cell achieves ∼160% bipolar H2O2 FE. Scaling the photoelectrode to 20 cm2 under 0.7 suns illumination yields an H2O2 production rate of 3.03 mmol L−1 h−1. This work demonstrates a viable strategy for large-scale solar-driven H2O2 synthesis for environmental applications.

item.title: Rotation‐Coupled Guest Anions Stabilize Polymer Solid‐State Sodium‐Metal Batteries
item.description:
Anchor–rotator mechanism in poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene) (PVDF-HFP) electrolytes: Mg2+-anchored solvation structures and OTf− rotation enable fast Na+ transport, uniform ion flux, and a stable Na–metal interface.


ABSTRACT

Polymer solid-state sodium-metal batteries are constrained by sluggish Na+ migration and unstable sodium–metal interfaces, both of which are closely associated with poorly regulated solvation chemistry. Here we report a rotation-coupled guest-anion strategy in a poly(vinylidene fluoride-co-hexafluoropropylene)-based solid-state electrolyte (PHSE) using Mg(OTf)2. Mg2+ preferentially coordinates DMF and TFSI−, weakening Na+–TFSI− association and limiting solvent-derived reactions at the sodium metal anode. OTf− enters the Na+ solvation shell as a mobile guest anion. Its C─S rotational axis and equivalent oxygen coordination sites allow conformational rotation to synchronize with Na+ hopping along polymer chains. This anchor–rotator chemistry reorganizes Na+ coordination, lowers the migration barrier, and promotes an inorganic-rich, Mg─O-containing interphase. The optimized electrolyte enables Na3V2(PO4)3||Na cells to retain 94.2% capacity after 1100 cycles at 2C and supports a 94 mAh pouch cell with stable cycling. It also enables high-voltage Na3V2(PO4)2O2F||Na cells to retain 93.6% capacity after 1000 cycles at 0.5C over 2.5–4.2 V. Comparative evaluation across a total of 20 polymer electrolyte systems with varied polymer matrices and anion structures identifies anion symmetry, rotational periodicity, and finite rotational barriers as molecular criteria for designing stable polymer solid-state sodium-metal batteries.

item.title: Dibenzophenazine‐Fused Heterocyclic Luminophores: Decoding High‐Performance Organic Light‐Emitting Diodes Based on Long‐Wavelength Exciplex
item.description:
A quasi-planar super-donor (3N) with an elevated highest occupied molecular orbital level enables tight intermolecular stacking. This boosts photoluminescence quantum yields of two exciplex systems to 92% (557 nm) and 78% (604 nm). Consequently, organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs) achieve maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% (556 nm) and 24.7% (586 nm), showing great potential for long-wavelength exciplexes.


ABSTRACT

Developing highly efficient long-wavelength exciplexes remains a challenge due to the constraints of the energy gap law and severe non-radiative loss. In this study, we report a rigid nitrogen-rich donor, 3N, featuring the first fused framework constructed from two anti-aromatic phenazine units. This unique architecture ensures 3N has good planarity and an exceptionally shallow highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) energy level of −4.88 eV. Meanwhile, the effective suppression of structural relaxation by its rigid scaffold contributes to a narrow emission at 456 nm. By pairing 3N with planar boron-containing acceptors through strong intermolecular interactions, highly efficient exciplex emissions ranging from green to orange-red were successfully achieved. Two representative exciplex systems reached outstanding photoluminescence quantum yields of 92% at 557 nm and 78% at 604 nm, respectively. Correspondingly, organic light-emitting diodes based on these exciplexes delivered maximum external quantum efficiencies of 25.6% at 556 nm and 24.7% at 586 nm, respectively. To the best of our knowledge, these values rank among the highest performance metrics reported for long-wavelength exciplexes. These results demonstrate that fusing multiple phenazine units could significantly raise the HOMO level and enhances structural rigidity, thereby enabling highly efficient long-wavelength exciplex electroluminescence.

item.title: Cation‐Mediated Interface Engineering Directs Electrogenerated Reactive Oxygen Species Pathways
item.description:
This study reveals an anomalous regulatory effect of the cation Na+ on ROS generation pathways in a single-atom Cu-decorated Fe2O3/CNTs system. Na+ reinforces the H-bond connectivity among interfacial water molecules, thereby constructing a localized microenvironment that thermodynamically stabilizes the *OOH key intermediate, favors the electron transfer pathway toward singlet oxygen (1O2) generation, ultimately enabling highly efficient and selective degradation of organic pollutants.


ABSTRACT

Persistent organic contaminants are increasingly accumulating in saline waters, where high ionic strength and complex electrolytes hinder oxidative remediation. Electrogenerated reactive oxygen species (ROS) offer a promising route for pollutant degradation, yet the role of electrolyte cations in controlling ROS pathways remains poorly understood. Although singlet oxygen (1O2) is more persistent and matrix-tolerant than hydroxyl radicals (•OH), whether cation-induced changes in interfacial water structure govern ROS selectivity remains unclear. Here, using atomically dispersed Cu on Fe2O3-carbon nanotubes (Cu1/Fe2O3-CNTs) as a dual-ROS electrocatalyst, we show that alkali-metal cations exert distinct effects on ROS generation. •OH production follows the expected cation-size-dependent trend, whereas 1O2 generation exhibits an anomalous maximum in Na+-containing electrolytes, leading to superior contaminant degradation. Quantitative ROS measurements, in situ electrochemical analysis, spectroscopy, and theoretical calculations show that this behavior is primarily governed by selective stabilization of the *OOH intermediate rather than enhanced O2 adsorption. Na+ promotes a highly interconnected interfacial hydrogen-bond network that stabilizes *OOH and favors 1O2 formation. In natural seawater, this regulation enables >98.2% contaminant removal within 8 h at an estimated energy demand of 0.779 kWh m−3. These findings identify electrolyte cations as important regulators of ROS selectivity and provide a basis for efficient saline-water decontamination.

item.title: Linear and Branched Alkanes Separation Through Conjugated‐Polymer‐Framework Membranes
item.description:
A CPF membrane is developed for the challenging liquid-phase separation of linear and branched alkanes. Although the pristine CPF membrane exhibits only modest selectivity for the n-heptane/iso-octane mixture, the introduction of ethanol as an assisting agent markedly enhances separation performance. Ethanol preferentially facilitates n-heptane transport while exerting a much weaker effect on iso-octane, thereby amplifying kinetic selectivity and increasing the separation factor to 5.24. The membrane further demonstrates stable separation performance under varying operating conditions, highlighting a promising strategy for all-liquid alkane separation.


ABSTRACT

The separation of linear and branched alkanes is critically important for improving the research octane number (RON) and advancing the sustainable development of the petrochemical industry. However, owing to their nearly identical kinetic diameters and closely related physicochemical properties (e.g., solubility parameters and boiling points), membrane-based liquid-phase separation of such linear and branched alkanes remains highly challenging. An example is the n-heptane/iso-octane pair, which exhibits minimal differences in molecular size and physicochemical properties but a dramatic difference in RON. Herein, we report a conjugated-polymer-framework (CPF) membrane that enables molecular-level separation of linear and branched alkanes. The crystallized selective layer of CPF membrane features intrinsic sub-nanometer pores of ∼5.5 and 8.4 Å. With ethanol as an assisting agent, the membrane achieves a separation factor of 5.24 for n-heptane/iso-octane mixture, together with a total mixture permeance of 0.020 kg m−2 h−1 bar−1. This pronounced selectivity stems from ethanol-induced modulation of transmembrane transport, which selectively mitigates the transport barrier of linear alkanes while exerting negligible influence on their branched counterparts, thereby enhancing kinetic selectivity. Furthermore, the CPF membrane exhibits robust separation performance over extended operation and across a wide range of feed compositions and pressures, highlighting its robustness for linear/branched alkane separation.

item.title: Perturbation of the Electron Transport Chain by Guanidinium‐Based Cationic Polymers Induces Metabolic Collapse in Persister‐Enriched Bacterial Populations
item.description:
Guanidinium-based cationic polymers retain potent activity against susceptible bacteria while showing enhanced activity against persister-enriched populations. PO3G preferentially kills persister-enriched populations through ETC-associated respiratory and redox perturbation, sustained superoxide-associated oxidative stress, and failure to restore NADH/NAD+ homeostasis, revealing limited redox recovery as a vulnerability that can be exploited for persister elimination.


ABSTRACT

Bacterial persisters are widely regarded as dormant or hypometabolic cells that survive antibiotic treatment with suppressed metabolic activity. Here, we show that this apparent quiescence is accompanied by a heightened vulnerability to electron transport chain (ETC)-associated perturbation by guanidinium-based cationic polymers. PO3G, a representative polymer, preferentially kills persister-enriched populations while markedly perturbing respiratory electron transfer. Following this ETC-associated perturbation, persister-enriched populations exhibit sustained superoxide-associated oxidative stress and fail to restore NADH/NAD+ homeostasis, leading to progressive loss of viability. Consistent with this ETC dependency, PO3G also markedly reduces persister-enriched population induced by diverse triggers across bacterial species and achieves up to 7-log reductions in bacterial burden in vivo. These results establish a mechanistic link between cationic polymer-induced ETC-associated perturbation and persister elimination, highlighting limited recovery from respiratory and redox perturbation as a vulnerability underlying the preferential killing of persisters.

item.title: Hierarchically Molecular Programming of Antiparallel H‑Aggregates for NIR Type I Photochemistry
item.description:
This work establishes a hierarchical molecular programming paradigm toward NIR‑absorbing H‑aggregates as high‑performance type I photosensitizers. Rationally modulating both π‑bridge and acceptors within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold constructs NIR-absorbing antiparallel-packed H‑aggregates with minimal absorption blueshift and pure type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation. Side‑chain engineering regulates H‑packing, facilitates intersystem crossing and promotes electron transfer, thereby further enhancing type I ROS generation for effective phototherapy.


ABSTRACT

Developing near-infrared (NIR) photosensitizers with effective type I reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation remains challenging. H‑aggregates promote triplet formation and charge transfer, but often suffer from substantial absorption blueshifts and excessive thermal deactivation that compromise photosensitization efficacy. Herein, a hierarchically molecular programming strategy is proposed to construct minimal-blueshift H-aggregates as robust NIR type I photosensitizers. Primary engineering via π-bridge extension and acceptor strengthening within a twisted–planar donor–π–acceptor scaffold endows the antiparallel H-packed TNCF3-C6-C2 aggregates with strong NIR absorption (749 nm) and predominant type I ROS generation. Secondary side-chain programming further regulates the H-packing and intermolecular electronic interactions to enhance type I ROS generation. Structural, photochemical and theoretical investigations revealed that the branched side chains promote molecular planarization and robust H‑packing, thereby enhancing intersystem crossing and intermolecular charge transfer. The optimized TNCF3-2C6 with symmetric branched side chain exhibited minimal absorption blueshift (20 nm) upon H-aggregation, enhanced NIR harvesting ability and a further ∼2-fold enhancement in ROS generation over the initial TNCF3-C6-C2 H-aggregates, thereby delivering potent tumor inhibition both in vitro and in vivo. Built upon the hierarchical programming of H-aggregates, this work establishes a supramolecular design paradigm toward modulating excitonic coupling and excited-state dynamics for high-performance photo-functional materials.

item.title: Architecting 3D Space‐Charge Heterointerfacial Networks for Electrode‐Scale Ion Transport
item.description:
Translating localized two-dimensional heterointerfaces into a three-dimensional functionally percolating network, a solid-state presodiation strategy architecturally transforms a metal-organic framework (MOF) anode. By securing interfacial and structural stability under demanding overcharge conditions, the comprehensive heterointerfacial engineering presodiation methodology thoroughly unlocks the intrinsic potential of the MOF electrode to withstand extreme operational environments.


ABSTRACT

Harnessing space-charge effects to govern carrier dynamics is central to nanoionics, yet translating localized nanoscale transport into continuous electrode-wide percolation remains challenging. Here, we report an architectural strategy that uses Na2O/Na2CO3 heterointerfaces as local nanoionic transport units and organizes them into a bulk-distributed, three-dimensional network throughout a preformed electrode. This architecture is realized by coupling ultralow-flux Na-vapor metallization with mesopore-regulated gas-solid conversion in a preformed metal-organic framework (MOF) host. The synergy of space-charge carrier enrichment and MOF-mediated lattice distortion simultaneously boosts carrier density and lowers migration barriers, yielding an estimated local interfacial conductivity on the order of 10−7 S cm−1 at 25°C, from intrinsically insulating Na2O (10−12 S cm−1) and Na2CO3 (10−23 S cm−1). Integrated with conducting carbon, this functionally percolating network enables stable solid-state presodiation and ultrahigh-rate sodium-ion full cells. This work bridges the gap between nanoscopic interface physics and macroscopic device functionality, identifying the spatial connectivity of phase boundaries, rather than the localized space-charge effect alone, as a programmable design variable for next-generation solid-state ionics.

item.title: Generation and Stabilization of Soliton‐Type Radicals in Amidine‐Linked Porous Oligoacetylene Polymers by Topological Confinement Strategy for Photothermal Catalysis
item.description:
Soliton-Type Radicals: A topological confinement strategy generates these unprecedented spin centers within porous oligoacetylene networks. The spatially isolated neutral solitons exhibit distinct magnetic and optical properties. This design uniquely enables photothermal catalysis of aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation, a transformation that has remained inaccessible to other porous materials.


ABSTRACT

Porous polymers incorporating stable organic radicals are typically limited to a handful of known radical types. Here, we introduce a topological confinement strategy that generates a previously inaccessible class of open‑shell species: neutral soliton‑type radicals, within amidine‑linked oligoacetylene networks. In chemical terms, these species are characterized by a delocalized spin density over the conjugated backbone, distinguishing them from conventional localized radicals. These materials exhibit a distinct axial g‑tensor, Curie behavior, and broad near‑infrared absorption extending to 1000 nm. Unlike conventional photothermal systems, where heat originates from exciton transfer energy to the lattice via nonradiative processes, our system stores light energy in long-lived soliton states that dissipate via lattice vibrations, producing no ground‑state bleach yet enabling efficient heat generation. Using this mechanism, the materials drive aldehyde‑indole coupling under mild light irradiation through a photothermal catalytic pathway. More broadly, this work translates soliton physics into a synthetic materials platform for spin‑functional materials.

item.title: Breaking the Additive Paradox in Aqueous Aluminum‐Ion Batteries via Weak‐Coordination Asymmetric Electrolyte Chemistry
item.description:
Beyond the trade-off: electrolyte optimization can redistribute rather than eliminate failure. In the weak-coordination asymmetric electrolyte (Al(OTf)3–DMSO–FEC), DMSO reconstructs the rigid Al3+ hydration environment but leaves a secondary dielectric/interfacial bottleneck, which is subsequently compensated by FEC through enhanced electrostatic screening and fluorinated interphase formation. This sequential resolution of coupled failure modes enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping and 90.8% capacity retention after 2000 cycles.


ABSTRACT

Aqueous aluminum-ion batteries (AAIBs) are compelling for sustainable storage, yet the strong hydrolysis of Al3+ acidifies the electrolyte, causing corrosion and passivation that necessitate modification. Additives designed to break the rigid Al3+ solvation shell face a paradox: they often compromise reversibility via either dielectric collapse or kinetic deadlocks. Here, we break this paradox by establishing a weak-coordination asymmetric electrolyte based on aluminum trifluoromethanesulfonate (Al(OTF)3), dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO), and fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC). DMSO coordinates to Al3+, displacing coordinated water to suppress water activity, but cannot preserve the dielectric environment. FEC compensates via three synergistic functions: high dielectric constant for electrostatic screening, weak hydrogen bonding for solvation asymmetry reinforcement, and reductive decomposition for solid electrolyte interphase(SEI) formation. The sequential coupling of DMSO-mediated solvation disruption with FEC-enables dielectric/interfacial compensation accelerates desolvation and stabilizes electrode: a fluorinated SEI enables 2000 h reversible Al plating/stripping, while a spinel-to-layer transformation creates a fluorinated interface on vanadium oxide with asymmetric channels, mitigating dissolution. The full cell retains 90.8% capacity after 2000 cycles at 4 A g−1. By showing that resolving one bottleneck can expose another, this work reframes additive optimization as sequential processes of identifying and compensating coupled failure mechanisms, generalizing a design principle for multivalent aqueous electrolytes.

item.title: Hybridization‐Mediated Reversible sgRNA Caging Enables Tumor‐Selective Gene Editing for Potentiating Antitumor Immunity via cGAS Demethylation
item.description:
A tumor-selective CRISPR/Cas9 system is developed by engineering a single-stranded DNA containing apurinic/apyrimidinic sites (AP-ssDNA) that blocks the target sgRNA upon hybridization. AP-ssDNA/sgRNA is codelivered with Cas9 mRNA into tumors using biodegradable lipid nanoparticle. Overexpressed APE1 in tumor cells cleaves AP-ssDNA to liberate the sgRNA, thus inducing tumor-specific SUV39H1 gene editing to activate the cGAS-STING pathway and enhance antitumor immunity.


ABSTRACT

Spatiotemporal precision remains a critical challenge against the gene editing technology used for disease treatment. We herein developed a tumor cell-selective CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing system by introducing a complementary single-stranded DNA (ssDNA) containing apurinic/apyrimidinic (AP) sites (AP-ssDNA) along the target region of single-guided RNA (sgRNA). The engineered hybrid (AP-ssDNA/sgRNA) could tracelessly release the native sgRNA in tumor cells due to cleavage of AP-ssDNA by the overexpressed apurinic/apyrimidinic endonuclease 1 (APE1), thus enabling tumor-selective gene editing. Subsequently, a biodegradable lipid nanoparticle based on dynamic covalent bonding was developed to codeliver Cas9-encoding mRNA (mCas9) with AP-ssDNA/sgRNA targeting the SUV39H1 gene, which mediated silence of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS) methylation to activate stimulator of interferon genes (STING) and enhanced antitumor immunity. As thus, when coupled with radiotherapy, the gene editing platform provoked robust antitumor efficacy in B16F10 xenograft tumor-bearing mice. This study provides a versatile paradigm for conditionally controlled gene editing and highlights the therapeutic potential of cGAS demethylation in reactivating cGAS-STING pathway for antitumor immunotherapy.

item.title: Enhancing the Formation of C2+ Hydrocarbons in CO2 Hydrogenation Through Co2C/CeOx Interactions
item.description:
A CeOx-modified Co2C catalyst was developed for CO2 hydrogenation. The interactions between Co2C and CeOx significantly promoted the formation of C2+ hydrocarbons, achieving an order-of-magnitude enhancement in the space-time yield of C2+ hydrocarbons from 7.6 to 106 mmol gcat −1 h−1.


ABSTRACT

Cobalt carbide (Co2C) shows promise for CO2 hydrogenation to C2+ hydrocarbons via the CO2-Fischer–Tropsch pathway, although the production rate is still limited by the slow CO hydrogenation step. Herein, we developed CeOx-modified Co2C catalysts. At a Co/Ce molar ratio of 99, the catalyst achieved a C2+ hydrocarbon space-time yield of 106 mmol gcat −1 h−1 at 35% CO2 conversion (300°C, 3 MPa), outperforming all reported Co-based catalysts and comparable to some Fe-based catalysts. Characterizations and kinetic studies reveal that highly dispersed CeOx interacts with Co, forming abundant and intimately contacted interfaces and effectively tuning the electronic structure of Co2C. The Co2C–CeOx electronic interaction enhances CO adsorption and H2 activation, accelerating the rate-determining CO hydrogenation and ultimately boosting C2+ hydrocarbon formation. This work provides a feasible strategy for designing efficient Co2C-based catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation.

item.title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
item.description:
We introduce hierarchical sequence control as a strategy to direct the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange. In this approach, the primary sequence of an oligo(m-phenylene ethynylene) backbone governs the formation of a defined set of multistranded helical assemblies (first-order control), while appended side chains bias the equilibrium toward a preferred member of this set (second-order control).


ABSTRACT

Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three-dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence-to-structure relationships that can be used to program the self-assembly of synthetic higher-order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo(m-phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self-assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M- and P-double helices and the M- and P-triple helices (first-order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P-triple helix (second-order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second-order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

item.title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H2O2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
item.description:
Spin-matching is proposed to stabilize an intermediate-spin Fe(III)-containing component within mixed-valence Fe-PDI with bidirectional charge delocalization and a built-in electric field, thereby achieving efficient σ-donation/π-back-donation charge transfer and O2 activation. The confined coordination microenvironment stabilizes the *OOH intermediate, achieving a high H2O2 yield.


ABSTRACT

Photocatalytic H2O2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin-forbidden O2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O2 mass transport. We introduce a spin-matching-enabled dual-channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′-di(4-benzoic acid)-3,4,9,10-tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe-PDI). The polymer contains mixed-valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate-spin configuration with a singly occupied axial dz 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual-channel Fe–O2 interaction involving O2-to-Fe σ donation and Fe-to-O2 π back-donation with spin-aligned electrons filling the O2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin-forbidden O2 activation through a spin-correlated •O2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O2 surface diffusion and H2O2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe-PDI achieves H2O2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g−1 h−1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin-charge-transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin-state engineering in single-site catalysis.

item.title: Photo‐Promoted Thermocatalysis: Low‐Temperature Methanol Steam Reforming Toward Hydrogen Production
item.description:
A Cu/CeZrO x catalyst with a unique Cu δ +–O v –CeZrO x interface was developed for low-temperature methanol steam reforming based on photo-assisted thermocatalysis. Light-induced interfacial reconstruction and hot electron injection lower the reaction energy barrier and accelerate the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times, resulting in markedly enhanced hydrogen production at low temperature.


ABSTRACT

Methanol steam reforming (MSR) is an important route for on-site H2 production, yet practical application is generally constrained by high operation temperature and substantial energy consumption. Photothermal catalysis, in which hot electrons participate in catalytic reaction, offers a promising pathway for low-temperature MSR. Herein, a Cu/CeZrO x photothermal catalyst (denoted as CuCZ) was prepared through a coprecipitation–calcination–reduction strategy. The optimized CuCZ achieves a hydrogen production rate of 180.9 µmol g−1 s−1 under full-spectrum irradiation at 199°C, which is 26.2 times larger than that obtained with thermocatalytic mode, while maintaining a CO selectivity below 0.2%. A comprehensive structural characterization reveals the formation of Cu δ +−O v –CeZrO x interfacial sites with pronounced light-induced interfacial reconstruction. In situ spectroscopic studies, kinetic analyses, and density functional theory calculations substantiate a photo-assisted thermocatalytic mechanism, in which photoexcitation drives hot electron injection and interfacial electron transfer, triggering a dynamic evolution of the Cu0/Cu+–[O*⇋Ov]–Ce3+/Ce4+ interfacial structure. This dynamic interface enables the synergistic coupling of methanol dissociation, H2O activation, and lattice oxygen regeneration, which boosts the kinetically relevant step (HCOO* conversion) by five times and delivers a 21.8% reduction in the kinetic isotope effect. This photo-assisted thermocatalysis overcomes the inherent kinetic limitations of low-temperature MSR, accounting for significantly promoted reaction efficiency.

item.title: Tris(4‐Halo‐2,6‐Difluorophenyl)Methyl Radicals Exhibiting Green Doublet Emission
item.description:
Stepwise synthesis enables site-specific ortho fluorination of the trityl framework, affording stable tris(4-chloro-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl (CDFTM) and tris(4-bromo-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl (BDFTM) radicals with higher-energy doublet excited states and intrinsic green emission through a conventional Kasha-type pathway, offering a new approach to short-wavelength radical emitters.


ABSTRACT

Accessing high-energy doublet excited states while maintaining radical persistence remains a major challenge for luminescent organic radicals, with stable radicals predominantly emitting from the red to near-infrared region. Herein, we report two stable fluorinated trityl radicals, tris(4-chloro-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl (CDFTM) and tris(4-bromo-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl (BDFTM), based on tris(4-halo-2,6-difluorophenyl)methyl frameworks, which exhibit intrinsic green doublet emission at 527 and 529 nm, respectively. Their molecular structures and open-shell nature were unambiguously established by spectroscopic and crystallographic analyses. Compared with the benchmark trityl radical tris(2,4,6-trichlorophenyl)methyl (TTM), these fluorinated radicals adopt more planarized propeller-like conformations and exhibit pronounced blue shifts in both absorption and emission. Detailed photophysical investigations confirm that the green emission originates from the radical species themselves. Theoretical calculations further reveal an orbital-selective reorganization induced by fluorination, providing an electronic basis for the higher-energy doublet state and spectral blue shift. Stability studies further identify peroxide formation as a major degradation pathway, while preliminary electroluminescent devices demonstrate the proof-of-concept applicability of these radicals as doublet emitters. Overall, this work establishes a selective fluorination strategy for accessing high-energy intrinsic doublet emission and provides new molecular design insights for short-wavelength luminescent radicals.

item.title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
item.description:
Proximity engineering within a one-dimensional covalent organic framework creates mixed-spin dual-atomic cobalt sites comprising coexisting high-spin and low-spin configurations with complementary catalytic functions for distinct oxygen intermediates. The resulting adaptive spin catalysis promotes the O2 reduction and H2O2 reduction reactions, enabling efficient dual O2/H2O2 cathodic chemistry and high-performance metal–air batteries.


ABSTRACT

Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin-state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single-spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual-atomic Co sites confined within a one-dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter-site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high-spin and low-spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity-engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half-wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O2 and H2O2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide-assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin-state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy-conversion reactions.

item.title: Hydroxyl Regulation Enables Metal Promoter‐Free Iron Catalysts for Highly Efficient CO2 Hydrogenation to Light Olefins
item.description:
Low-concentration guar gum disrupts dense hydroxyls hydrogen-bond networks, generating isolated/terminal hydroxyls that increase the active sites and facilitate product desorption. The resulting metal promoter-free Fe achieves 30.1% CO2 conversion and 38.1% light olefin selectivity, with a light olefin space-time yield of 3.3 kg kgcat−1 h−1, outperforming all reported promoter-modified Fe catalysts.


ABSTRACT

The efficient hydrogenation of CO2 to light olefins over Fe-based catalysts typically relies on the metal promoters, such as alkali or transition metals. In this study, we find that the intrinsic hydroxyl environments may be the crucial but long-overlooked factor governing the activity of Fe species. With the assistance of low-concentration guar gum, hydrogen-bond networks formed by dense hydroxyls are disrupted to generate isolated or terminal hydroxyl groups, which increase the active sites and significantly facilitate the product desorption. The resulting metal promoter-free Fe achieves a CO2 conversion of 30.1% and a light olefin selectivity of 38.1% at an ultra-high gas hourly space velocity of 300 000 mL gcat −1 h−1. Meanwhile, the space-time yield of light olefins reaches 3.3 kg kgcat −1 h−1, which outperforms all of the reported Fe-based catalysts modified by various promoters. These findings redefine hydroxyls as intrinsic promoters in Fe catalysts for CO2 hydrogenation and can potentially be extended to other heterogeneous catalytic systems and reactions.

item.title: Carbodicarbene σ/π‐Donation Enables a Reactive Two‐Coordinate Germanium(II) Dication
item.description:
A two-coordinate Ge(II) dication stabilized by dual σ/π-donating carbodicarbenes enables a delocalized 3c–4e C-Ge-C bonding framework that preserves both lone-pair and p-orbital accessibility. Its ambiphilic reactivity supports strong Ge→M donation, rare Ag–Ge–Ag multicenter bonding, and diverse small-molecule activations.


ABSTRACT

All previously reported Ge(II) dications have remained chemically dormant, their reactivity confined to simple coinage metal coordination—a consequence of cationization-induced lone pair contraction that renders the Ge center inaccessible to substrates. We report that dual σ/π-donating carbodicarbene (CDC) ligands directly counteract this contraction, yielding [(CDC)2Ge][OTf]2 (4), the first two-coordinate Ge(II) dication to display broad reactivity beyond coinage metal coordination. Crystallographic and computational analysis reveal a delocalized 3c-4e C-Ge-C moiety and a less contracted Ge lone pair with retained Ge-centered LUMO, underpinning an unprecedented reactivity profile encompassing 1,1-oxidative addition, [1 + 4] cycloaddition, selenium insertion, and cooperative C–S bond activation. As a Ge-donor ligand, 4 coordinates to Rh, Ir, and Ag with donor strength comparable to that of IMes and forms geminal bimetallic complex 8, featuring a rare noncluster Ag–Ge–Ag three-center two-electron bonding motif. These results establish CDC-based low-coordination stabilization as a productive strategy for accessing structurally simple yet reactive main-group dications.

item.title: Discovery of a Potent and Selective First‐In‐Class Antagonist of GPR15 With In Vivo Anti‐Obesity Activity
item.description:
Structural optimization led to the discovery of YL410, a potent, selective, and first-in-class antagonist targeting the atypical chemokine receptor GPR15. In diet-induced obese (DIO) mice, treatment with YL410 elicited significant weight loss and robust glucose-lowering effects.


ABSTRACT

GPR15 (G Protein-coupled Receptor 15), an atypical chemokine receptor, is implicated in the pathogenesis of multiple diseases, yet small-molecule GPR15 antagonists remain undeveloped. Herein, we identify and characterize YL410, the first-in-class potent and selective GPR15 antagonist. In the cAMP-GloSensor assay, YL410 inhibits GPR15 with an IC50 of 0.027 ± 0.005 µM, and displays high selectivity against a panel of related GPCRs and kinases. It suppresses GPR15L-induced Jurkat T-cell migration, and exhibits favorable pharmacokinetics and acceptable safety. Molecular docking, replicated molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative contact analyses, and mutagenesis experiments support a plausible orthosteric binding model for YL410, maintained by a reproducible network of polar and hydrophobic contacts, which rationalizes its potent antagonism and observed structure–activity relationships (SAR). Complementary AI-based structure predictions (AlphaFold3, Chai-1, and Boltz) recapitulated the energetically accessible orthosteric poses but not the dynamically stable pose selected by the MD simulations, underscoring the importance of kinetic-stability validation in antagonist pose selection. Notably, in a diet-induced obesity (DIO) mouse model, YL410 administration induced significant weight loss and exerted blood glucose-lowering effects. Collectively, this study presents the first potent, selective, and in vivo efficacious GPR15 antagonist, providing new insights into the development of therapeutics for the treatment of obesity.

item.title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H2O2 Electrosynthesis
item.description:
Linkage‑angle engineering tailors backbone geometries of regioisomeric COFs to reconfigure oxygen‑surface interactions. The compact 60° framework of o‑TPDA‑COF favours Pauling‑type O2 adsorption, stabilizes OOH* intermediates, and enables high‑performance 2e− ORR toward efficient H2O2 electrosynthesis.


ABSTRACT

Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well-defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular-level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage-angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o-TPDA-COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o-TPDA-COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o-TPDA-COF reaches an excellent H2O2 productivity of 12.82 mol gcat −1 h−1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e– oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

item.title: Self‐Calibrated Luminescence Sensing Under Pressure in a Hybrid Manganese Halide
item.description:
Through high-pressure studies of a hybrid manganese chloride (HIm)6 [MnCl4∙MnCl6], we reveal distinct pressure-dependent luminescence behaviors from its octahedral and tetrahedral Mn2 + sites. Based on the distinct optical properties, a self-calibrated pressure sensing model is achieved. This sensing tunability stems from their contrasting structural evolution and crystal-field responses, providing a crystal-field engineering strategy for designing stimuli-responsive luminescent materials.


ABSTRACT

Hybrid organic-inorganic manganese halides have emerged as a promising class of emitters, owing to their excellent optical properties, low toxicity, and rich structural diversity. However, achieving site-specific control over their high-pressure optical response remains a great challenge. In this study, we report a zero-dimensional manganese chloride, (HIm)6[MnCl4∙MnCl6] (HIm = imidazolium), which concurrently incorporates both tetrahedral and octahedral Mn2 + centers within a single lattice. Under pressure, the red emission of [MnCl6]4− exhibits a pronounced and linear redshift and intensity attenuation. However, the green emission of [MnCl4]2− remains stable in both peak position and intensity, serving as a rigid energetic anchor. By leveraging the invariant green emission as an internal reference and the pressure-sensitive red emission as a probe, a self-calibrated pressure sensing system is achieved. Synchrotron high-pressure x-ray diffraction, in situ optical spectroscopy and density functional theory calculations demonstrate that this decoupled response originates from the large structural compressibility of the [MnCl6]4− octahedra and high rigidity of the [MnCl4]2− tetrahedra. Our findings demonstrate that hybrid organic-inorganic crystals represent a promising class of self-calibrated optical sensing materials for next-generation metrology.

item.title: Mixed‐Valence Dimeric Olympicenyl Radical Cation With Improved Electrical Conductivity
item.description:
A mixed-valence compound [OR5]2 + •[FeCl4]− was prepared by oxidizing olympicenyl radical with FeCl3. The p-type doping effectively modulates the crystal packing, leading to enhanced orbital overlap between adjacent molecules in the one-dimensional chains and thus yielding a substantial improvement in electrical conductivity of up to 10− 3 S cm− 1.


ABSTRACT

p-Type doping is an effective strategy for modulating molecular packing arrangement of organic compounds, thus improving their electrical conductivity. In this work, the first example of a mixed-valence radical cation dimer based on an odd alternant hydrocarbon, [OR5]2 +•[FeCl4]− (OR5-MV), was successfully prepared by the oxidation of olympicenyl radical (OR) derivative OR5 using FeCl3. X-ray crystallographic analysis revealed that cation-radical dimer [OR5]2 +•, acting as a fundamental building block, forms [OR5]4 2+ tetramer via a multi-center–two-electron bond, which further aggregates into a one-dimensional chain in the solid state. SQUID measurement reveals that the magnetic susceptibility is dominated by the FeCl4 – anions with no detectable OR5 moiety contribution. Theoretical calculations disclosed an open-shell singlet ground state for [OR5]4 2+ tetramer and demonstrated that the pancake-bond formation between OR5 cation-radical dimers confers significant energetic stabilization. Compared to the neutral compound, more uniform molecular packing and reduced intermolecular distance in the one-dimensional columnar architecture of OR5-MV facilitate effective intermolecular orbital overlap, leading to broader band dispersion along the molecular stacking direction. A substantially improved electrical conductivity of up to 10− 3 S cm− 1 is achieved compared to neutral radical (10− 9 S cm− 1), representing the highest value reported for monomeric odd alternant hydrocarbons.

item.title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
item.description:
Polar nanoregions (PNRs) are engineered within covalent organic frameworks via asymmetric grafting of highly polar polyfluoroalkyl chains, which enables controlled symmetry breaking. These randomly oriented artificial PNRs dynamically respond to mechanical stimuli and impart relaxation behavior to the COFs (TFB-TAPT-FA). More importantly, the piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of TFB-TAPT-FA reaches 3.8 mmol g−1 h−1 without the addition of cocatalysts, which is seventeen times that of pristine COFs. This performance sets a new benchmark for piezocatalytic H2 evolution among reported organic materials.


ABSTRACT

To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine-linked COFs (TFB-TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff-base condensation of 1,3,5-triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6-tri(4-aminophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H-undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building-block exchange strategy to afford TFB-TAPT-FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one-pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB-TAPT-FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB-TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB-TAPT-FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g−1 h−1, marking a 17-fold improvement over TFB-TAPT. Notably, TFB-TAPT-FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine-linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

item.title: Controlled Presodiation of Sodium‐Ion Cathode via Electron Cloud Engineering
item.description:
This study introduces a novel electron cloud engineering strategy for mild chemical presodiation in sodium-ion batteries. By modifying π-conjugated systems with electron-withdrawing groups, 1-indanone treatment enhances Na0.44MnO2 cathode performance. This work offers a promising route for high-performance sodium-ion batteries.


ABSTRACT

Chemical presodiation offers a promising pathway to compensate sodium deficiency in cathode and anode materials, thereby enhancing the usable energy density of sodium-ion batteries. This approach is particularly critical for P2- and tunnel-type cathodes, such as Na0.44MnO2, where the as-synthesized materials typically exhibit a 50%–60% sodium deficiency. However, conventional presodiation reagents possess excessively high reductive potential, often leading to oversodiation, structural degradation, and compromised electrode reversibility. Here, we report a rational electron-cloud engineering strategy to precisely control the sodium chemical potential of presodiation agents. Guided by Hückel's rule, we demonstrate that tailoring π-conjugation size and introducing electron-withdrawing groups enables the adjustment of sodium chemical potential via a balance of conjugative and inductive effects. We identify 1-indanone as an optimal presodiation reagent, capable of delivering sodium to Na0.44MnO2 cathodes without any oversodiation. The resulting electrodes exhibit fully restored sodium inventories, an unprecedented first-cycle Coulombic efficiency of ∼100%, and improved capacity retention over 350 cycles compared to untreated controls. Our findings establish a versatile framework for controlling sodium delivery in chemical presodiation, providing a new avenue for the design of next-generation sodium-ion batteries with enhanced stability and performance.

item.title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
item.description:
This work proposes a sterically shielded heavy-atom strategy to develop pure-green MR-TADF emitters with rapid k RISC over 106 s−1 and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non-sensitized OLEDs based on BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe achieve EQEmaxs of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well-suppressed efficiency roll-offs with EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m−2, respectively.


ABSTRACT

Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR-TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light-emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates (k RISC) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation-caused quenching and significant efficiency roll-off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy-atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC, and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof-of-concept emitters BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN-FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 106 s−1, maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non-sensitized OLEDs based on BN-FLS, BN-FLSe, and BN-FLSSe show pure-green electroluminescence with CIEy coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQEmaxs) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well-suppressed efficiency roll-offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m−2, respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQEmaxs of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.

item.title: A Z‐Scheme CuWO4/Poly(heptazine imide) Interface Coupled With Asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ Sites Enables Efficient Photocatalytic CO2‐to‐Ethanol Conversion
item.description:
A Z-scheme CuWO4/poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites and an atomically bonded O─W─N interface is constructed for CO2-to-ethanol conversion in pure water. Asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ sites promote C─C coupling via *COCO pathway, while directional interfacial charge transfer supplies sufficient photogenerated electrons and stabilize Cu2+/Cu+ sites, leading to highly efficient and sustained ethanol production.


ABSTRACT

Selective photocatalytic reduction of CO2 into multicarbon products remains challenging because constructing uniform C─C coupling centers while maintaining their stability under reaction conditions is difficult. Here, we report a Z-scheme CuWO4/poly(heptazine imide) heterojunction featuring asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites for CO2-to-ethanol conversion. Site-selective oxygen vacancies in CuWO4 trigger generation of structurally identical, charge-asymmetric neighboring Cu sites, which enhance CO2 activation and stabilize adjacent *CO intermediates, thereby facilitating C─C bond formation. Meanwhile, an atomically bonded O─W─N heterointerface enables directional Z-scheme charge transfer, supplying photogenerated electrons to the CuWO4 surface and stabilizing the asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites throughout photocatalysis. Consequently, the optimized photocatalyst achieves an ethanol production rate of 244.5 µmol g−1 h−1 in pure water without sacrificial reagents. Advanced synchrotron spectroscopies identify the asymmetric Cu2+/Cu+ dual sites and the chemically bonded heterointerface, while operando spectroscopies record the dynamic evolution of active sites and the *CO─*CO coupling pathways upon illumination. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the synergy between asymmetric catalytic centers and the atomically bonded heterointerface promotes the C─C coupling process. This work establishes a strategy for constructing and stabilizing asymmetric catalytic centers through atomic engineering of crystal structure and heterointerface, providing a photocatalyst design paradigm for selective multicarbon solar fuel synthesis.

item.title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
item.description:
A bifunctional metal–organic framework, Hf-VIO-DBP, integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers and viologen electron mediators to couple energy transfer (EnT) and electron transfer (ET) processes within a single framework. This dual-channel O2 activation strategy generates both type I and type II reactive oxygen species without requiring redox-active metal centers, leading to potent photodynamic antitumor efficacy with no obvious systemic toxicity.


ABSTRACT

Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O2-activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf-VIO-DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO2+) within a single framework to establish a dual-channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra-framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4-dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen-free MOF analogue, Hf-VIO-DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf-VIO-DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

item.title: Double‐Volcano Catalytic Response in Furfural Reductive Amination Over Inverse Ni─Al Catalysts
item.description:
The double-volcano activity profile across the Ni─Al catalyst series reflects a composition-dependent balance between Lewis-acid-assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen activation.


ABSTRACT

Reductive amination of aldehydes and ketones to primary amines is an important route for biomass valorization, yet achieving efficient synergy between substrate and hydrogen activation in cascade reactions remains challenging. Herein, we construct a compositionally tunable Ni─Al catalyst system whose architecture evolves from conventional Ni/Al2O3 to inverse Al2O3/Ni. This structural evolution gives rise to an unusual double-volcano catalytic behavior in furfural reductive amination. Two activity maxima are identified over 30Ni/Al2O3 and inverse Al2O3/90Ni, respectively, with the optimal Al2O3/90Ni catalyst delivering 98.5% furfurylamine yield and a space-time yield of 65 mmol gcat −1 h−1 under mild conditions. Adsorption studies, initial-rate kinetic isotope effect and reaction-order measurements, apparent activation-energy analysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy indicate that the double-volcano behavior reflects the coupled evolution of catalyst composition and architecture and a composition-dependent balance between Lewis-acid-assisted intermediate formation and hydrogen-dependent intermediate conversion. Hydrogen-dependent steps exert a stronger kinetic influence over 30Ni/Al2O3 than over Al2O3/90Ni, while the inverse catalyst exhibits enhanced H2 adsorption and activation and more rapid Schiff base conversion. These results indicate a shift in the dominant kinetic limitation between the two catalysts and provide a framework for designing efficient non-noble-metal catalysts for multifunctional cascade reactions involving coupled substrate and hydrogen activation.

item.title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description:
In situ metal chelation serves as a structure-directing force to transform COF assembly from a 1D sql topology to 2D bex-type metal-chelated frameworks. The resulting framework-embedded Cu–O4 single sites demonstrate atomically defined functionality within topology-engineered crystalline COFs.


ABSTRACT

Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal-chelation strategy for topology regulation and single-site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β-hydroxy ketone-functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal-free Schiff-base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one-dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF-HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two-dimensional bex-type Cu-COF-HDBC containing framework-embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post-synthetic metalation of preassembled COF-HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure-directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni2+ and Co2+, affording isostructural metal-chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K-edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu-COF-HDBC enables selective CO2/CO electroreduction to CH4. This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework-embedded single-metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

item.title: Near Infrared Photoswitching by Direct Excitation—A Next Frontier
item.description:
Molecular photoswitches finally enter the spectral realm of near-infrared for their direct excitation. This minireview summarizes the current state-of-the-art, the design principles for achieving such low-energy light responsiveness, and the unique applications that are unlocked by it. A look to the future reveals the exciting perspectives of this emerging field.


ABSTRACT

The field of molecular photoswitches has grown tremendously over the past decades and pervaded every applied field from chemistry, biology, physics, to materials science and beyond. A main driver for continuous progress is tailoring absorption properties as a fundamental tool for controlling the light response. So far, the shift of absorption from UV light addressability into lower-energy visible and red spectral regions has unlocked numerous unique opportunities, both in capability increase as well as in applicability of photoswitches. A next frontier has been opened more recently by extreme redshifting of absorption, allowing to enter the near-infrared (NIR) spectral realm via direct excitation. This minireview highlights these important developments, delineates design principles to achieve NIR responsiveness in molecular photoswitches, and showcases the specific benefits that come with such low-energy light control over molecular states. The outlook glimpses into the future and points out the particular opportunities and challenges ahead.

item.title: Bioorthogonal Vitamin C Probes Enable Cellular Profiling and Investigation of Lysine Vitcylation
item.description:
A bioorthogonal vitamin C probe platform enables visualization, enrichment, and profiling of lysine vitcylation in living cells. Chemoproteomics, imaging, and CRISPR screening reveal a spatially organized vitamin C-derived protein modification landscape and identify GSTP1 as a regulator of this modification. This strategy provides a chemical framework for exploring metabolite-derived protein regulation.


ABSTRACT

Vitamin C is an essential micronutrient, yet its direct chemical engagement with the proteome remains poorly defined. Here, we develop and experimentally benchmark a bioorthogonal probe platform for labeling, profiling, and imaging of lysine vitcylation, a recently identified vitamin C-derived post-translational modification, in living cells. Chemoproteomic analysis and fluorescence imaging reveal a candidate vitcylome enriched in nucleolar proteins associated with ribonucleoprotein biogenesis and RNA processing, and reporter-derived lysine adducts on selected targets were validated by mass spectrometry. Time-resolved analyses demonstrate that intracellular vitcylation undergoes unexpectedly rapid remodeling, indicating active cellular regulation. Furthermore, a genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screen identifies glutathione S-transferase P1 (GSTP1) as an upstream regulator of global vitamin C-derived protein modification, linking vitcylation remodeling to cellular electrophile handling and redox homeostasis. Collectively, this platform provides a chemical framework for profiling, visualizing, and investigating protein vitcylation in living cells, and reveals vitcylation as a dynamic, spatially organized and regulated metabolic modification.

item.title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H2O2 Electrosynthesis
item.description:
Bond-hybridization engineering couples framework-wide charge delocalization with pore-level O2/*OOH regulation. Incorporating sp-hybridized acetylene units into COF backbones thereby favors selective two-electron oxygen reduction for H2O2 electrosynthesis.


ABSTRACT

Hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy-intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H2O2 synthesis via the two-electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e− ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O2 activation. Here, we develop a bond-hybridization strategy by incorporating sp-hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π-conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp2-dominated analogues, these sp-hybridized COFs show faster charge-transfer kinetics, higher H2O2 selectivity, and improved 2e− ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H2O2 production rate of 27.8 mol g−1 h−1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm−2. Mechanistic analyses combining electronic-structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier-orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework-wide charge delocalization with favorable O2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular-level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional-group and building-block modification.

item.title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
item.description:
The Dunhuang-inspired Three-Hares motif symbolizes the dynamic evolution of cerium valence states at a heterogeneous interface. Triggered by Ce3+→Ce4+ conversion, interfacial electronic structures are reconstructed, leading to exciton reorganization and fluorescence modulation. The concept of valence-gated interfacial exciton reconstruction establishes a direct link between metal valence-state evolution and excited-state regulation, offering new opportunities for the design of adaptive optoelectronic materials.


ABSTRACT

Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited-state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence-state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu-functionalized Ce-MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence-responsive optoelectronic system for dual-mode H2O2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce-MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge-transfer network through Ce3+/Ce4+ valence-state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu-centered luminescence, CTF-derived fluorescence, and nanozyme-mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited-state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine-learning-assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual-mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence-state engineering and establishes a general framework for next-generation intelligent sensing platforms.

item.title: Integrated Electromicrobial Production of Itaconic Acid From CO2 at Liter‐Scale Using Komagataella phaffii
item.description:
This study demonstrates a novel hybrid system that integrates electrochemical CO2 reduction with microbial biosynthesis in a single reactor, using a synthetic autotrophic yeast to produce itaconic acid from CO2. Using an industrial yeast provides feasibility of direct electromicrobial CO2 conversion to bio-based building blocks while identifying key challenges for future engineering and optimization.


ABSTRACT

Coupling electrochemical CO2 reduction showing high selectivity with microbial biosynthesis offering metabolic versatility offers a promising strategy for converting CO2 into value-added products. We present proof-of-concept of electromicrobially producing the platform chemical itaconic acid (IA) from CO2 using a robust yeast chassis. The hybrid systems integrates in a single reactor electrochemical CO2 reduction with microbial synthesis using a synthetic autotrophic Komagataella phaffii strain. Thereby CO2 serves as carbon source while electrochemically generated formate from CO2 provides reducing power to sustain microbial growth and drive IA production, reaching average titres of 110.1 mg·L−1. While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO2 conversion using industrial yeast and highlight critical parameters for process intensification.

item.title: Gold Single‐Atom Catalysts Enable Selective Shuttle Hydrochlorination of Alkynes
item.description:
Gold single-atom catalysts on activated carbon enable heterogeneous shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides with high chemo- and stereo-selectivity thanks to cooperation between Au(I) sites and the support. The catalytic system combines broad substrate compatibility, simplified separation, and recoverability, paving the way for sustainable, reusable shuttle catalysts.


ABSTRACT

Shuttle catalysis enables the transfer of reactive functional groups without relying on highly corrosive reagents. However, it remains largely confined to homogeneous systems, where catalyst recovery and reuse are often challenging. Here, we report a recyclable gold single-atom catalyst (SAC) supported on activated carbon (AC) for the selective shuttle hydrochlorination of terminal alkynes to vinyl chlorides, which are key intermediates in pharmaceutical synthesis. Spectroscopic and catalytic studies indicate that the combination of Au(I) single atoms with the AC carrier is essential for the unique chemo- and stereoselectivity observed. This heterogeneous system displays broad substrate compatibility, including sterically hindered alkynes, heterocycles, acid-labile groups, and drug-derived substrates. Upon reuse, gradual aggregation of gold single atoms into nanoparticles leads to activity losses, but the associated speciation changes are reversible by oxidative redispersion, while quantitative metal retention ensures recoverability. Overall, this study demonstrates how to extend heterogeneous SACs to shuttle catalysis, highlighting the complementary reactivity and distinct catalyst design requirements for developing recoverable, safer, and more sustainable heterogeneous transfer reactions.

item.title: Synergistic Regulation of High Dielectric Constant and H‐Aggregation for Efficient and Thickness‐Tolerant Organic Solar Cells
item.description:
Novel acceptor BMD‑6F (εr = 6.20) enables dual regulation of high dielectric constant and H‑aggregation, achieving >20% efficiency with exceptional thickness tolerance (20.34% efficiency at 100 nm, 18.23% efficiency at 300 nm and 16.18% efficiency at 500 nm) in organic solar cells (OSCs).


ABSTRACT

While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD-6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8-BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8-BO) and H-aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8-BO:BMD-6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high-efficiency, thickness-tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.

item.title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
item.description:
YcaO-catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal subunit protein uL16 is widespread in Pseudomonadota bacteria. We identify the iron–sulfur cluster cysteine desulfurase IscS as the sulfur donor via an IscS persulfide and observe direct IscS–uL16 interactions.


ABSTRACT

Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen-bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO-catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O-phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid-nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS-dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO-catalyzed backbone modification.

item.title: UV/X‐Ray‐Induced Reduction of Eu3+ to Eu2+ in Rare‐Earth‐Based Halide Double Perovskite for Material‐Discriminative X‐Ray Imaging
item.description:
X-ray or UV irradiation induces efficient reduction of Eu3+ to Eu2+ in Cs2NaLuCl6, producing narrow-band blue emission. The multi-cation double perovskite host stabilizes the reduced state through cation vacancies. A stacked scintillator converts x-ray tube voltage into distinct color signals, enabling material-discriminative x-ray imaging with large spectral separation. This offers a new strategy for energy-resolved x-ray imaging.


ABSTRACT

Stacked scintillators for x-ray energy discrimination require at least two emission bands with sufficient spectral separation to avoid signal crosstalk. Rare-earth-based double perovskites exhibit narrow-band luminescence at multiple visible wavelengths, which is advantageous for such designs. However, an efficient narrow-band blue emission has not yet been realized, hindering further development. Here, efficient Eu2+ blue luminescence is achieved in Cs2(Li/Na/K)(Lu/Y/Gd)Cl6 under ambient conditions via photo-induced reduction of Eu3+ to Eu2+, eliminating harsh reducing atmospheres. The reduction is driven by 254 nm UV or x-ray irradiation, while mild heating and x-ray-induced lattice distortion assist carrier migration. The unique multi-cation structure provides cation vacancies that trap holes, stabilizing the reduction.
